items.title: Empleados Meta dicen cuentas de Lula se vieron limitadas durante elecciones Brasil: Folha
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Empleados de Meta reconocieron en comunicaciones internas que las cuentas de Instagram del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se vieron afectadas negativamente por las restricciones impuestas durante las elecciones de Brasil, informó el viernes el periódico "Folha de S.Paulo", citando mensajes a los que tuvo acceso.
items.body:
Empleados de Meta reconocieron en comunicaciones internas que las cuentas de Instagram del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se vieron afectadas negativamente por las restricciones impuestas durante las elecciones de Brasil, informó el viernes el periódico "Folha de S.Paulo", citando mensajes a los que tuvo acceso.
Según el informe, los mensajes también reconocían que la plataforma recomendaba el perfil del candidato opositor, el senador Flávio Bolsonaro, así como su canal de WhatsApp.
Meta (META.O) no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios.
Lula se enfrentará a Bolsonaro en un balotaje el 25 de octubre, tras el resultado, mejor de lo esperado, obtenido por el senador en la primera vuelta celebrada a principios de este mes.
El equipo de Lula afirmó a principios de esta semana que presentaría una denuncia ante la Organización de los Estados Americanos alegando que Meta, propietaria de Instagram, WhatsApp y Facebook, manipuló las redes sociales durante las elecciones de Brasil.
Según el partido de Lula, algunas de sus publicaciones aparecieron sin botón para compartir, sufrieron una reducción de su alcance y presentaban historias que impedían las reacciones y el intercambio, además de aparecer sin audio o reproducirse a velocidad acelerada.
Un magistrado del máximo tribunal electoral de Brasil ordenó el jueves a la empresa que no limitara injustificadamente el alcance del contenido político relacionado con ambos candidatos hasta el final de la campaña de la segunda vuelta.
La resolución también estipulaba que Meta AI, el chatbot de inteligencia artificial de la empresa, no debe favorecer a ninguno de los candidatos a la hora de generar contenido relacionado con las elecciones.

items.title: Chinese online retailer Temu agrees to data privacy restrictions to settle Texas lawsuit, documents say
items.author: Jody Godoy, David Shepardson
items.creator: Jody Godoy, David Shepardson
items.summary: Chinese online retailer Temu has agreed to settle data privacy claims raised by Texas and will restrict how it handles personal data from shoppers in the state, according to documents made public Friday.
items.body:
Chinese online retailer Temu has agreed to settle data privacy claims raised by Texas and will restrict how it handles personal data from shoppers in the state, according to documents made public Friday.
Temu faces several lawsuits from US states concerned that the company unlawfully harvests US user data that could be accessed by the Chinese government. Texas is the first to resolve those claims. It is also the first time the company has agreed to keep personal data on US servers and restrict when it can be sent to China, Texas officials said.
Temu also agreed to conduct annual independent product safety testing to identify products containing dangerous chemicals and materials. Temu must remove any products found to contain dangerous materials, terminate the seller and its affiliated stores, notify affected Texas consumers, and issue full refunds.
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said the settlement also requires Temu "to implement rigorous new product audits and safety standards to protect consumers from dangerous materials in products, including clothing and children’s items."
He added it will prevent Temu from collecting and using Americans' data.
Temu had more than 82.4 million active users in the United States as of September 2023, Paxton's office said.
Temu will pay $3 million to the state as part of the settlement and Texas said failure to abide by various data security provisions would result in a potential $8 million penalty each year a violation occurs.
Several states sued Temu in the wake of reports alleging Temu and parent company PDD Holdings < PDD.O > used invasive mechanisms in their apps.
Temu, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment, denied wrongdoing in the settlement documents, and will also be required to hire a third party cybersecurity auditor to examine the app’s code for malware and spyware, one of the main concerns that spurred Texas to sue in February.
Under the terms of the settlement, Temu agreed to send only data necessary to fulfilling a transaction, such as shipping addresses, to China.
Texas alleged that Temu used code that allows an inappropriate level of access to users’ devices. Temu has denied the allegations.
items.raw_description: Chinese online retailer Temu has agreed to settle data privacy claims raised by Texas and will restrict how it handles personal data from shoppers in the state, according to documents made public Friday.

items.title: Edited image of transgender councillor shared online
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: An image of a transgender Green Party councillor in Britain has been edited to give her more masculine features.
items.body:
An image of a transgender Green Party councillor in Britain has been edited to give her more masculine features.
The altered image, shared on X and Facebook , shows Eden Hills, councillor for Little London and Woodhouse , in the northern English city of Leeds, with facial hair.
The original image was a screenshot taken from a video uploaded to the Leeds Green Party’s Instagram account on May 8, in which Hills delivers a speech upon being elected as a representative for the ward. That does not show a moustache.
Reuters analysed the altered photo with Google’s SynthID, an AI detection tool, which concluded the image was created using the tech company's generative AI models. The tool works by detecting a hidden watermark contained in AI-generated or AI-modified images created by Google models.
Hills also told Reuters in a phone call on October 14 that the image is not genuine.
Hills was elected as councillor for the Green Party on May 7 with 2,617 votes , more than half of the votes cast among six candidates, according to Leeds City Council.
Verdict: Misleading. The image is altered to depict Hills with an added moustache.
This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more  about our fact-checking work.

items.title: Russia's Rosatom targets year-end nuclear start-up at Turkey's Akkuyu
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom expects the first reactor at Turkey's Akkuyu nuclear power plant to achieve its first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction before the end of this year, Rosatom head Alexei Likhachev said on Friday.
items.body:
Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom expects the first reactor at Turkey's Akkuyu nuclear power plant to achieve its first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction before the end of this year, Rosatom head Alexei Likhachev said on Friday.
"We remain on track for the planned physical start-up in the second half of December... We hope that before the end of the year the Turkish unit will transition from the construction phase to the start-up phase," he said.
Moscow and Ankara signed an agreement in 2010 to build a nuclear power plant with four Russian VVER-1200 reactors, but the project has faced repeated delays and bureaucratic hurdles.
Rosatom began construction of the Akkuyu plant in 2018. The commissioning schedule has been repeatedly pushed back from its original 2023 target.
After Moscow launched military action in Ukraine in 2022, pressure on the project increased. Although Rosatom was not targeted by Western sanctions, risks related to payments and other issues remain.
Physical start-up involves fuel loading and achieving first criticality, the reactor's first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction. The next major milestone is grid connection and the start of electricity generation.
Likhachev also reported progress in talks with potential partners for the Akkuyu.
He said he had discussed the matter the previous day with Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar, who attended the Russian Energy Week forum.
"We have developed a menu of possible arrangements for a Turkish investor. The choice is primarily up to the Turkish government. I hope that following our meeting, Mr Bayraktar will brief the country's leadership and that the right decisions will be taken."
The Akkuyu project, costing more than $20 billion, is financed by Russia. Rosatom, its sole owner, can sell up to a 49% stake to a partner to share the investment burden.
In April, Rosatom [USN:L6N4140Z0 TEXT:"said"] it started new talks with Turkish companies on joint ownership of Akkuyu after the Iran war spurred interest in such assets.

items.title: Kenya reports third Ebola case, a close relative of first two patients
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Kenya reported its third Ebola infection on Friday, in a woman it said was closely related to the first two patients.
items.body:
Kenya reported its third Ebola infection on Friday, in a woman it said was closely related to the first two patients.
The 65-year-old had been in quarantine since October 6, the health ministry said in a statement.
"Once she developed fever, sore throat and malaise, she was isolated and specimen collected for testing," it added. "She was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care improving her chances of recovery."
Authorities say Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo — the [USN:L8N45Z1AX TEXT:"second-largest"] outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths.
Kenya's [USN:L8N45S0GY TEXT:"first recorded case"] was a man who had been ill in Congo for about a month, then travelled by road to Uganda and flew to Nairobi on October 3.
That Kenyan man was driven to hospital by a relative and died on October 5.
The health ministry said the second patient was in a stable condition and there was still no evidence the disease was spreading in the wider community.
FEARS OF SCREENING LAPSES Ebola's spread to Kenya has raised concerns about lapses in screening systems. The first patient managed to cross the border between Congo and Uganda, which has been closed since May, and then pass through Nairobi's busy Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.
Kenyan authorities say they have contacted 127 out of the 130 people known to have come into contact with the first patient. They had all been placed into quarantine and efforts were under way to trace the remaining three.
Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected people, whether living or dead. The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding.
The outbreak in Congo was declared in mid-May but may have started months earlier. It is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which there are currently no approved vaccines or treatments.
Uganda reported Ebola cases in May and June but was declared free of the virus in August. A doctor who returned to France in June from Congo tested positive but there have been no further cases there.

items.title: SpaceX's spectrum deal still leaves it far from rivaling telecom giants
items.author: Harshita Varghese
items.creator: Harshita Varghese
items.summary: SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more.
items.body:
SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more.
Starlink became a money maker by offering internet service in rural and sparsely populated areas, where it faced little competition, as well as changing to easy-to-set-up home packages at a competitive price. Mobile will be harder.
Cities are particularly tough places for mobile telephony and are technologically challenging for mobile-to-satellite connections.
The rocket and satellite company will likely need to invest heavily in ground infrastructure, customer service, handset subsidies and promotions — costly parts of the wireless business in which AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile already have extensive operations.
Building a network would cost more than $80 billion, according to TD Cowen, and add to SpaceX's capital demands as it pours money into its Starship rocket program, AI infrastructure, and Terafab chip factory.
"It's just hard to imagine that this is all going to get done within a decade," said Julie Zhu, a research analyst at MoffettNathanson. "In the decade or so leading up to 2023, the big three spent about $650 billion in capex to build in networks that ostensibly were already finished."
Most phones have small antennas and limited transmitting power that make reliable satellite connections more challenging because satellites orbit hundreds of kilometers above Earth, much farther away than cell towers.
"There are too many pitfalls for satellite to be the only source of data," said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy.
SPACEX PUBLISHES HYBRID SPACE-TERRESTRIAL PLAN SpaceX has called the latest deal, in which [USN:L4N45U1O2 TEXT:"it acquired 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain"] at a price a source pegged at nearly $8 billion, a "critical next step" for the nascent Starlink Mobile to provide high-speed mobile service.
"Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere," including "indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between", SpaceX said, announcing the purchase.
SpaceX has received regulatory authorization for up to 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites and plans to deploy traditional terrestrial infrastructure such as antennas on towers and rooftops — a hybrid approach rather than pure satellite-to-phone — it laid out in a regulatory filing made public last week.
In a Starlink Mobile system, satellites could connect directly to mobile phones and indirectly by relaying signals through ground infrastructure. This is similar to the technology of a partnership between Starlink and T-Mobile, which provides the terrestrial network while Starlink supplies the satellite connectivity that fills in where there are no towers. That is a T-Mobile-branded service.
SpaceX in theory could strike a deal with one of the big three companies to use its ground infrastructure, what is known as a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO, arrangement. However, SpaceX "appear to be going after a more build-your-own approach to a terrestrial network since nobody will offer them wholesale MVNO," Sag said.
SpaceX would need several times more spectrum to match the holdings of the three big mobile companies, although current spectrum might be enough to start. "It is for a company with zero mobile subscribers, plenty of runway, and a robust device/equipment ecosystem," TD Cowen said.
Would-be rivals dismissed the idea that the effort was an imminent threat.
T-Mobile Chief Technology Officer John Saw said SpaceX's spectrum would not be enough to match the capacity and performance of established mobile networks, while Katie Magnotta, Verizon's associate vice president of corporate communications, said, "A company can have billions of dollars of spectrum, but if they do not have the network to use it, it's just empty airwaves."
items.raw_description: SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more.

Oct 16 : SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more.
Starlink became a money maker by offering internet service in rural and sparsely populated areas, where it faced little competition, as well as changing to easy-to-set-up home packages at a competitive price. Mobile will be harder.
Cities are particularly tough places for mobile telephony and are technologically challenging for mobile-to-satellite connections.
The rocket and satellite company will likely need to invest heavily in ground infrastructure, customer service, handset subsidies and promotions — costly parts of the wireless business in which AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile already have extensive operations.

Building a network would cost more than $80 billion, according to TD Cowen, and add to SpaceX's capital demands as it pours money into its Starship rocket program, AI infrastructure, and Terafab chip factory.
"It's just hard to imagine that this is all going to get done within a decade," said Julie Zhu, a research analyst at MoffettNathanson. "In the decade or so leading up to 2023, the big three spent about $650 billion in capex to build in networks that ostensibly were already finished."
Most phones have small antennas and limited transmitting power that make reliable satellite connections more challenging because satellites orbit hundreds of kilometers above Earth, much farther away than cell towers.
"There are too many pitfalls for satellite to be the only source of data," said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy.
SPACEX PUBLISHES HYBRID SPACE-TERRESTRIAL PLAN
SpaceX has called the latest deal, in which it acquired 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain at a price a source pegged at nearly $8 billion, a "critical next step" for the nascent Starlink Mobile to provide high-speed mobile service.
"Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere," including "indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between", SpaceX said, announcing the purchase.
SpaceX has received regulatory authorization for up to 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites and plans to deploy traditional terrestrial infrastructure such as antennas on towers and rooftops — a hybrid approach rather than pure satellite-to-phone — it laid out in a regulatory filing made public last week.
In a Starlink Mobile system, satellites could connect directly to mobile phones and indirectly by relaying signals through ground infrastructure. This is similar to the technology of a partnership between Starlink and T-Mobile, which provides the terrestrial network while Starlink supplies the satellite connectivity that fills in where there are no towers. That is a T-Mobile-branded service.
SpaceX in theory could strike a deal with one of the big three companies to use its ground infrastructure, what is known as a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO, arrangement. However, SpaceX "appear to be going after a more build-your-own approach to a terrestrial network since nobody will offer them wholesale MVNO," Sag said.
SpaceX would need several times more spectrum to match the holdings of the three big mobile companies, although current spectrum might be enough to start. "It is for a company with zero mobile subscribers, plenty of runway, and a robust device/equipment ecosystem," TD Cowen said.
Would-be rivals dismissed the idea that the effort was an imminent threat.
T-Mobile Chief Technology Officer John Saw said SpaceX's spectrum would not be enough to match the capacity and performance of established mobile networks, while Katie Magnotta, Verizon's associate vice president of corporate communications, said, "A company can have billions of dollars of spectrum, but if they do not have the network to use it, it's just empty airwaves."

Source: Reuters

items.title: L'Allemagne devrait dévoiler la semaine prochaine un accord avec Nvidia sur l'IA-sources
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: L'Allemagne devrait annoncer la semaine prochaine la signature d'un accord de coopération avec le fabricant américain de puces Nvidia afin de développer l'utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle dans l'industrie allemande, ont indiqué vendredi des sources gouvernementales.
items.body:
L'Allemagne devrait annoncer la semaine prochaine la signature d'un accord de coopération avec le fabricant américain de puces Nvidia (NVDA.O) afin de développer l'utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle dans l'industrie allemande, ont indiqué vendredi des sources gouvernementales.
Les sources ont précisé que ce projet impliquerait d'autres partenaires que Nvidia et constituerait une contribution majeure à l'IA industrielle.
Le quotidien économique Handelsblatt, qui a été le premier à faire état de ce projet, a indiqué que cet [USN:L1N4610UA TEXT:"accord"] soutiendrait le développement d'outils d'IA physiques destinés à l'entraînement des robots et des véhicules autonomes, et contribuerait à la mise au point de modèles d'IA puissants à usage industriel.

items.title: El S&P 500 opera con leve baja, subidas de bancos contrarrestan el nerviosismo por la IA
items.author: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
items.creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
items.summary: El índice de referencia S&P 500 cotizaba con una leve baja el viernes, ya que la preocupación por el sector de la inteligencia artificial ejercía presión sobre las acciones de los semiconductores, pero una subida de los bancos limitaba las caídas generales.
items.body:
El índice de referencia S&P 500 cotizaba con una leve baja el viernes, ya que la preocupación por el sector de la inteligencia artificial ejercía presión sobre las acciones de los semiconductores, pero una subida de los bancos limitaba las caídas generales.
El sector de tecnología de la información del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) era el que más golpeaba al índice, con una caída del 0,9%.
CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , respaldada por Nvidia, perdía un 7,6% debido a la persistente preocupación por el endeudamiento del operador de centros de datos. Sus bonos sufrieron una fuerte venta masiva esta semana, lo que elevó sus rendimientos sobre el 15%.
* Otras empresas de "neocloud", como Nebius Group (NBIS.O) e Iren (IREN.O) , caían más de un 5,5% cada una.
* El sector de los semiconductores volvía a perder terreno: Micron Technology (MU.O) bajaba un 3,9% y Advanced Micro Devices (.AMD) , un 3,3%. El índice general de chips (.SOX) perdía un 1,8%, lo que lo sitúa ante la mayor caída porcentual en ocho sesiones desde la ola de ventas del "Día de la Liberación" en abril de 2025.
La mayoría de las acciones de gran capitalización también registraban caídas: Alphabet (GOOGL.O) y Meta (META.O) cedían un 1%, lo que presionaba al sector de servicios de comunicaciones (.SPLRCL) y al Nasdaq.
El retroceso de las acciones de chips de memoria a principios de esta semana, debido al temor por la competencia china y a la preocupación por la deuda de CoreWeave, "proporcionó a los inversores una excusa para reducir su exposición a todas las empresas relacionadas con la IA", dijo David Morrison, analista senior de mercados de Trade Nation.
A las 15:19 GMT, el índice S&P 500 (.SPX) perdía 22,23 puntos, o un 0,29%, a 7.721,83 unidades, mientras que el Nasdaq (.IXIC) bajaba 292,66 puntos, o un 1,10%, a 26.420,37 unidades. En tanto, el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) sumaba 176,81 puntos, o un 0,34%, a 52.354,50 unidades.
Por el contrario, la mayoría de los demás sectores del S&P 500 subían. El de materiales (.SPLRCM) era el que registraba la mayor alza porcentual, de un 1,6%, mientras que el sector financiero (.SPSY) ganaba un 1,1%.
Las subidas de Goldman Sachs (GS.N) y JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) impulsaban al Dow a su nivel más alto en más de un mes.
El S&P 500 y el Nasdaq se encaminaban a registrar pérdidas semanales, ya que la caída provocada por la inteligencia artificial, los resultados bancarios dispares y los datos de inflación mermaron la confianza a lo largo de la semana. El Dow, por su parte, se encaminaba a cerrar la semana al alza.
Los informes de esta semana sobre la inflación de los precios al consumo y al productor, más altos de lo esperado, han confirmado que las presiones sobre los precios se están traspasando desde la energía a otros productos.

items.title: Ryazan refinery halted processing at one primary unit after drone attacks, sources say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russia's Ryazan oil refinery has suspended operations at one of its primary crude distillation units following a drone attack in the region on Thursday, two industry sources told Reuters.
items.body:
Russia's Ryazan oil refinery has suspended operations at one of its primary crude distillation units following a drone attack in the region on Thursday, two industry sources told Reuters.
A big Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Ryazan region caused a fire to break out at an oil refinery, the regional governor Pavel Malkov said on [USN:L8N4610DI TEXT:"Thursday"].
The sources said on Friday that one of the oil refinery's main units, CDU-6, was halted following the attack. The unit had previously been suspended after another attack [USN:L8N4520GP TEXT:"last month"]. During the latest attack several refinery pipelines were also damaged.
The refinery has another three primary crude distillation units - CDU-1, CDU-3 and CDU-4 - which continue to operate and may be used during the CDU-6 outage, according to the sources.
Rosneft (ROSN.MM) , which owns the refinery, did not reply to a request for comment about the attack on the plant.
The Ryazan oil refinery, which feeds Moscow with fuel, has been attacked several times this year. The plant has a processing capacity of 17 million metric tons per year, or some 340,000 barrels per day. The refinery can produce 3.4 million tons of gasoline and 3.8 million tons of diesel per year.

items.title: Colts release veteran WR Darius Slayton
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have pulled the plug on the Darius Slayton experiment after less than a month.
items.body:
The Indianapolis Colts have pulled the plug on the Darius Slayton experiment after less than a month.
The Colts signed the veteran wide receiver on Sept. 22 and released him on Friday without ever putting him on the field.
Slayton, 29, was brought in for depth after the injury to Alec Pierce (heel) and due to his familiarity with quarterback Daniel Jones.
Slayton reportedly struggled to pick up the offense in Indianapolis and was further hampered by a knee injury.
He played for the New York Giants from 2019-25, catching 296 passes for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns in 106 games (78 starts).
--Field Level Media

items.title: EUA orientam autoridades a ficarem alertas a golpes baseados em IA antes das eleições de meio de mandato
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O FBI e a agência de defesa cibernética dos Estados Unidos, a CISA, estão alertando as autoridades eleitorais — e o público norte-americano — para que fiquem atentos a golpes baseados em inteligência artificial antes das eleições legislativas de meio de mandato do próximo mês.
items.body:
O FBI e a agência de defesa cibernética dos Estados Unidos, a CISA, estão alertando as autoridades eleitorais — e o público norte-americano — para que fiquem atentos a golpes baseados em inteligência artificial antes das eleições legislativas de meio de mandato do próximo mês.
Um alerta divulgado nesta sexta-feira pela CISA e pelo FBI afirmou que hackers podem tentar atrapalhar as eleições usando mensagens de texto e emails falsos com o objetivo de roubar senhas ou outros dados confidenciais.
O alerta afirma que “autoridades eleitorais, candidatos e suas organizações políticas são alvos atraentes para criminosos cibernéticos mal-intencionados”.
O alerta afirma que a “superinteligência” — um termo aprovado por Trump para se referir à IA — está permitindo que os hackers aprimorem seus emails e mensagens de texto fraudulentos para torná-los mais convincentes na aparência e no tom.
(Reportagem de Raphael Satter)

items.title: COP31 Les tortues caouannes, sentinelles du réchauffement en Méditerranée
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Sous un ciel baigné de lune, des bébés tortues sortent du sable sur la côte méditerranéenne turque et se hâtent vers la mer, dans un cycle naturel ancestral de plus en plus menacé par le changement climatique.
items.body:
Sous un ciel baigné de lune, des bébés tortues sortent du sable sur la côte méditerranéenne turque et se hâtent vers la mer, dans un cycle naturel ancestral de plus en plus menacé par le changement climatique.
Tout au long de la nuit, le biologiste marin Yakup Kaska et son équipe de bénévoles veillent sur les nids. Des cages pyramidales protègent les œufs enfouis dans le sable contre les renards qui parcourent les quatre kilomètres de la plage d’Iztuzu: une plage touristique le jour, un sanctuaire pour la conservation des tortues la nuit.
La tortue caouanne, qui pond sur les rivages de Méditerranée, est la mascotte de la COP31, la 31e conférence de l'Onu sur les changements climatiques que la Turquie accueillera du 9 au 20 novembre. La protection des écosystèmes marins figurera parmi les priorités de ce sommet organisé sur la côte, à Antalya.
LA TORTUE MARINE, BAROMÈTRE DU CLIMAT "Les tortues marines nous fournissent un système d'alerte très rapide", explique Ayfer Sirin, maître de conférences en écologie à l’université d’Uskudar, qui a mené des recherches approfondies sur les tortues caouannes. Selon elle, à la croisée de la terre et de la mer, ces animaux sont les témoins des bouleversements qui gagnent les écosystèmes côtiers et marins.
La température d’incubation détermine le sexe des nouveau-nés, les sables plus chauds favorisant la naissance de femelles.
Une étude doctorale de cinq ans menée à l’université de Pamukkale par Ayfer Sirin a mis en évidence un lien entre le réchauffement, une ponte plus précoce, une incubation plus courte et une proportion de femelles atteignant 70% parmi les nouveau-nés de la plage de Patara.
À Iztuzu, la température des nids a augmenté de près d'un degré Celsius en vingt ans, indique Yakup Kaska, ajoutant qu’une analyse plus large suggère que les femelles représentaient jusqu’à 80 à 90% des nouveau-nés dans de nombreuses populations de tortues marines.
À mesure que le sable se réchauffe, l’équilibre entre les sexes se fragilise. Si les mâles deviennent trop rares, la reproduction pourrait être compromise. Au-delà de 30°C, la chaleur accroît également le risque de mortalité des embryons, souligne Ayfer Sirin.
Les tortues caouannes sont classées comme "vulnérables" à l’échelle mondiale. Les populations méditerranéennes sont considérées comme de "préoccupation mineure", grâce aux progrès de la conservation, mais subissent de nouvelles pressions climatiques.
HABITATS TRANSFRONTALIERS Yakup Kaska souligne que les migrations des tortues illustrent la nécessité d’une coopération transfrontalière, car elles nichent parfois en Turquie et se nourrissent en Tunisie ou dans l’Adriatique. Raison de plus pour appeler les pays à unir leurs efforts afin de protéger la biodiversité méditerranéenne.
Le président de la COP31, Murat Kurum, ministre turc de l’Environnement, est allé dans ce sens lors d’une conférence sur les océans et les mers le mois dernier: "La protection des océans est une responsabilité que nous partageons tous. Nous appelons chaque partie à traduire cette responsabilité en actions audacieuses et concrètes: restaurer les écosystèmes et renforcer la résilience."
DES FILETS DE PÊCHE AUX DÉCHETS PLASTIQUES Les caouannes femelles reviennent généralement pondre, des décennies plus tard, sur la plage où elles sont nées. Mais certaines gagnent désormais des côtes plus au nord, où elles étaient autrefois rares, observe Yakup Kaska.
Iztuzu demeure un refuge essentiel: chaque saison, quelque 30.000 nouveau-nés émergent de centaines de nids et s’élancent vers la mer. Dans les flots, les nouveau-nés affrontent de nouveaux dangers: filets de pêche, bateaux et déchets plastiques.
À quelques pas de la plage d’Iztuzu, le centre Dekamer offre un refuge aux tortues blessées, soignées dans de grands bassins, notamment après avoir été heurtées par des hélices de bateaux.
Selon Yakup Kaska, 60% des tortues accueillies au centre ont au moins cinq morceaux de plastique dans leur système digestif.
"Jeter un sac en plastique à la mer, c’est comme tirer une balle sur les tortues."

items.title: EEUU insta a estar alerta ante engaños basados en IA de cara a elecciones de medio término
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El FBI y la agencia estadounidense de ciberdefensa CISA instaron a los responsables electorales y a la ciudadanía a mantenerse alerta ante los engaños basados en la inteligencia artificial de cara a las elecciones de mitad de legislatura del próximo mes.
items.body:
El FBI y la agencia estadounidense de ciberdefensa CISA instaron a los responsables electorales y a la ciudadanía a mantenerse alerta ante los engaños basados en la inteligencia artificial de cara a las elecciones de mitad de legislatura del próximo mes.
A continuación, más detalles:
Una alerta emitida el viernes por la CISA y el FBI advierte que los piratas informáticos podrían intentar perturbar las elecciones de mitad de legislatura mediante mensajes de texto y correos electrónicos falsos destinados a robar contraseñas u otros datos confidenciales.
La alerta señala que "los responsables electorales, los candidatos y sus organizaciones políticas son objetivos atractivos para los ciberdelincuentes malintencionados".
La alerta señala que la "superinteligencia" —un término aprobado por Trump para referirse a la IA— está permitiendo a los piratas informáticos perfeccionar sus correos electrónicos y mensajes de texto fraudulentos para que parezcan más convincentes.

items.title: KFC switch to Coke puts PepsiCo's food service ties in focus, analysts say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: KFC's decision to switch from Pepsi sodas to Coca-Cola at its US restaurants could raise questions about PepsiCo's other longstanding food service partnerships, analysts said, even as they expect the financial hit to be manageable.
items.body:
KFC's decision to [USN:L4N46120T TEXT:"switch"] from Pepsi sodas to Coca-Cola (KO.N) at its US restaurants could raise questions about PepsiCo's (PEP.O) other longstanding food service partnerships, analysts said, even as they expect the financial hit to be manageable.
The loss of KFC comes as PepsiCo grapples with sluggish demand and higher costs in North America, where a recovery in growth and margins is taking [USN:L6N45U0N9 TEXT:"longer than expected"] and has prompted the company to deepen cost cuts.
BofA analysts estimate the loss of the KFC account represents about $500 million in annual sales, equivalent to roughly a 3% hit to Pepsi Beverages North America's concentrate sales, while boosting Coca-Cola's North America sales by about 2.5%
Brokerage Jefferies says the bigger concern for PepsiCo is the "loss of brand interaction and public perception" rather than the immediate financial impact
"A longstanding Pepsi customer switching raises questions whether other accounts that have been historically off-limits are now up for grabs," Jefferies analysts said
"Investors see this (move) less as a seismic commercial loss for PepsiCo and more as the natural order of... (a brand) reasserting itself," says Richard Exon, founder and partner at Joint, an independent creative  agency

items.title: Data centers may benefit from massive rural utility loan, US official says
items.author: Leah Douglas
items.creator: Leah Douglas
items.summary: A record-breaking $3.3 billion loan from the U.S. Department of Agriculture to a power plant in Georgia's Monroe County could potentially benefit data centers in the state, the agency's head of rural development said in an interview with Reuters.
items.body:
A record-breaking $3.3 billion loan from the U.S. Department of Agriculture to a power plant in Georgia's Monroe County could potentially benefit data centers in the state, the agency's head of rural development said in an interview with Reuters.
The administration of President Donald Trump has [USN:L1N45K0VR TEXT:"supported"] the rapid expansion of data centers, despite their [USN:L6N42I0TN TEXT:"unpopularity "]with communities concerned about water use and utility costs. Democrats are attempting to capitalize on that [USN:L6N45916H TEXT:"discontent "]in November's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"].
Glen Smith, the USDA's Under Secretary for Rural Development, said in the Thursday interview that he hopes to secure more funding for such projects.
Here are more details:
The USDA announced on Tuesday the loan to Oglethorpe Power Corporation, the largest ever given under the agency's Rural Utilities Service.
Smith said the plant will serve 38 rural utility cooperatives and support growing industry in the state, including potentially data centers.
Last year, Google purchased nearly 1,000 acres of land in Monroe County for a data center.
Oglethorpe spokesperson Blair Romero said in an email, "This facility is not dedicated to serving a data center. The new facility will help our Member cooperatives meet growing electricity demand across their communities."
Smith said he plans to meet with congressional appropriators next week and request more money for such loans. "We have almost $8.6 billion in requests, and we're only into our fiscal year one month," he said.
Smith said rural areas can benefit from data centers, "but you have to have the infrastructure in place. and that's where rural utilies and rural development comes into play."
Data centers are driving US electricity use to [USN:L6N42Q137 TEXT:"record highs "]and in some regions, demanding more power than grids can supply.
The Trump administration has not sought to regulate data center construction, instead asking tech companies to [USN:L1N3ZR10I TEXT:"pledge"] not to pass on electricity costs to consumers.

items.title: Meta employees said Lula's accounts were hindered during Brazil election, Folha reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Employees at Meta acknowledged in internal communications that the Instagram accounts of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were negatively affected by restrictions during the country's election, newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported on Friday, citing messages it reviewed.
items.body:
Employees at Meta (META.O) acknowledged in internal communications that the Instagram accounts of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were negatively affected by restrictions during the country's election, newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported on Friday, citing messages it reviewed.
The messages also acknowledged the platform recommended the profile of challenger Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, as well as his WhatsApp channel, according to the report.
Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment
Lula will face Bolsonaro in a runoff on October 25, following a stronger-than-expected performance by the senator in the [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"first-round vote"] earlier this month
Lula's camp said earlier this week it would file a complaint before the Organization of American States alleging that Meta, which owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook, manipulated social media during Brazil's election
According to Lula's party, some of his posts appeared without a share button, suffered reduced reach, and had stories that prevented reactions and sharing, in addition to appearing without audio or playing at accelerated speed
A justice at Brazil's top electoral court on Thursday ordered the company not to unjustifiably limit the reach of political content related to both candidates through the end of the runoff campaign
The ruling also stipulated that Meta AI, the company's artificial intelligence chatbot, must not favor either candidate when generating election-related content

items.title: Chile's pension funds requested curbs on interest-rate bets before losses, Bloomberg reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Executives at Chile's pension funds appealed to regulators for curbs on volatile interest-rate derivatives before a downturn in US Treasuries left them with billions of dollars in losses, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.
items.body:
Executives at Chile's pension funds appealed to regulators for curbs on volatile interest-rate derivatives before a downturn in US Treasuries left them with billions of dollars in losses, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.
The report said that fund managers had flagged risks of positions that have since hit the system's most conservative fund hard. The losses have drawn criticism from some lawmakers and raised concerns among pensioners.
Chile's [USN:L3N3OP1TQ TEXT:"private pension system"] is managed by firms known as Administradoras de Fondos de Pensiones (AFPs), or pension fund administrators, which oversee five investment funds ranging from Fund A, the riskiest, to Fund E, the most conservative.
Earlier this week, the AFP Association's head of research, Roberto Fuentes Silva, attributed a decline in Fund E to rising US interest rates after Bloomberg reported that Chilean pension funds had posted losses of about $7.7 billion on interest-rate-related positions.
Executives managing these pension funds had asked regulators in private conversations to enforce rules on the stockpiling of volatile derivatives, Bloomberg's Thursday report said, citing people familiar with the conversations.
The lucrative nature of the trade meant the executives could not act independently without forgoing returns that rivals would continue to cash in, the report added.
Chile's pension regulator did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.
Chilean lawmaker Nelson Venegas from the opposition Socialist Party described the AFP losses as "very serious," accusing pension fund managers of putting workers' savings at risk and calling for tougher measures against those responsible.
Ximena Ossandón, a lawmaker from the right-leaning National Renewal party aligned with the [USN:L1N43N14S TEXT:"government"], said it was too early to draw conclusions and that authorities should first determine whether the AFPs had acted within existing regulations.
“We should wait to determine whether the investments were made within the permitted framework or not," Ossandón said in a statement.
The AFP Association has sought to reassure contributors, saying in a statement that pension fund performance should be assessed over the long term rather than based on short-term market fluctuations.
"A pension fund does not have losses or gains; rather, it experiences increases or decreases in its valuation," Fuentes Silva told local media.
Chile's current private pension system started in the early 1980s during the Augusto Pinochet dictatorship and relies solely on worker contributions managed by the AFPs.
The system has long faced criticism for generating relatively low pensions while AFP operators continue to post significant profits. After years of political debate, Congress approved a major [USN:L3N3OP1TQ TEXT:"pension reform"] in January 2025, with the rollout beginning in stages from August last year and continuing over several years.

items.title: US FDA sets up board to oversee drug exclusivity determinations
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The US FDA's drug evaluation department said on Friday it has formed a board to oversee and advise on exclusivity determinations made by the department, aiming to improve clarity and consistency of those decisions.
items.body:
The US FDA's drug evaluation department said on Friday it has formed a board to oversee and advise on exclusivity determinations made by the department, aiming to improve clarity and consistency of those decisions.
Here are more details:
FDA-granted exclusivity rewards innovation by giving newly approved drugs a period of market protection, before lower-cost generic competitors enter the market
The CDER (Center for Drug Evaluation and Research) exclusivity board will oversee certain exclusivity determinations, including whether and what type of exclusivity should be granted and the appropriate scope of grants, the agency said on Friday
The board will focus on 5-year new chemical entity exclusivity that is granted to a drug whose active ingredient has never before been approved by the FDA
It will also oversee 3-year new clinical trial exclusivity grants that are meant for drugs that use a previously approved active ingredient, but their approval relies on new clinical studies conducted or funded by the sponsor
It will advise on exclusivity for biological products too
The board will not review other types of exclusivity apart from the three, it said
The board also may evaluate and make recommendations regarding CDER's policies and practices relating to exclusivity and maintain records of exclusivity determinations

Oct 16 : Manchester City's players and supporters have grown closer since the club were found to have breached Premier League financial rules, head coach Enzo Maresca said on Friday, adding scrutiny had placed him under no additional stress.
An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal.
"I think (City centre back and captain) Ruben Dias said people do not like City winning, so that is why we like to win. That is a good message for everyone," Maresca said at a news conference.
"Since the noise, from my personal point of view, I can see the fans, the club, the team more together, for sure.

"There is noise around the club but we need to try to make our noise. That means win at Anfield, try to win tomorrow (against Ipswich). This is the way we can make our noise. A different kind of noise, we are not able to control that.
"I don't feel any kind of stress about the outside situation because it is something I don't control. I just focus on how we can try to win the next games."
City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday in their first match since the verdict before suffering a 4-2 home defeat by back-to-back Champions League winners Paris St Germain on Wednesday.
Maresca's side remain top of the Premier League with six wins from six matches and will look to bounce back from their midweek defeat when they host 10th-placed Ipswich Town on Saturday.
Asked whether he had sought advice from anyone outside the club to better understand the situation, Maresca said he had no need to do so.
"I spoke with the club a few times, they explained to me the situation, so the situation is very clear, and I trust the club 100 per cent, I trust the people that run the club and this is the reason why I joined the club," the Italian said.
Former City manager Pep Guardiola attended the PSG match, and Maresca said he caught up with him afterwards.
Maresca was part of Guardiola's coaching staff during City's treble-winning campaign before successful managerial spells at Leicester City and Chelsea.
"We were talking about the game, the first half, the second half. He was very happy to be at the stadium and then very positive about things he had seen during the game... This will always be his house," Maresca added.

items.title: 米財務省、ロシア政府系ファンドに軽油取引の決済円滑化要請＝ドミトリエフ特使
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Vladimir Soldatkin　Olesya Astakhova

[モスクワ　１６日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Vladimir Soldatkin　Olesya Astakhova

[モスクワ　１６日　ロイター] - ロシアの政府系投資ファンド、ロシア直接投資基金（ＲＤＩＦ）を率いるドミトリエフ大統領特別代表は１６日、トランプ米大統領とロシアのプーチン大統領が合意したロシア産ディーゼル（軽油）取引を巡り、米財務省から決済の円滑化を要請されたと明らかにした。また米ロ両国が、ロシアの小型原子力発電所を活用したデータセンター建設など、新たな共同事業について協議していることも明らかにした。 

ドミトリエフ氏はロシアの首都モスクワで開かれたエネルギー関連会議で、米財務省がＲＤＩＦに対し「決済の円滑化と実務的な問題の解決」を求めたとした上で、「ＲＤＩＦは全ての決済が効率的に行われ、資金が本来の受取先に確実に届くよう取り組む」と述べた。

同時に「制裁措置が幾重にも積み重なっているため、誰もが混乱しており、打開策を見いだすのが難しくなっている」と指摘。「制裁解除の方法を巡る検討はすでに始まっており、米国は現在、まさにその作業を進めている」と語った。

ドミトリエフ氏はまた、「ロシアと米国のデータセンター分野での共同事業についても協議している。小型原子力発電所の活用も含まれる」と述べた。詳細には触れなかった。

ウクライナは今月、ロシアのＩＴ大手ヤンデックスと銀行・テクノロジー大手ズベルバンクのデータセンターを攻撃した。ウクライナはこれを、自国施設へのロシア軍の攻撃に対する報復としている。  

米ロ協議で主要な役割を担うドミトリエフ氏は、鉱物資源やエネルギーを含む幅広い分野で野心的な合意を模索してきた。米政府はこれまで、こうした合意をウクライナ和平と結び付ける姿勢を示しており、ロシア政府は不満を表明してきた。和平合意は依然見通せない状況だ。 

ただ、ドミトリエフ氏はこの状況が変わりつつあるとの楽観的な見方を提示。「当然ながら進展は難しい。各方面から広範な抵抗がある。それでもディーゼルの事例が示すように、他の重要な取り組みを近く発表できると考えている。氷は実際に解け始めている」と語った。 

ドミトリエフ氏はこれまでにも、ロシア産ディーゼル供給を巡る米ロ合意は、両国間の一段の経済協力に道を開く可能性があるとし、今回のディーゼルを巡る合意が米ロ間の他の経済協力のモデルになり得るとの見方を示している。

また、故リンゼー・グラム上院議員が提案した対ロシア制裁法案（グラム法）について、ロシアと米国の投資協力を阻害するものと非難。「ロシアと米国の共同事業を明らかに阻害するほか、両国がエネルギー市場の安定化や世界市場で果たす役割が妨げられる」と語った。

トランプ米大統領は９日、ロシアのプーチン大統領と電話会談を行い、ロシアが米国と世界市場にディーゼルを供給することで合意したと発表。燃料価格の引き下げを狙った措置で、米政権はウクライナ戦争の戦費となるロシアの収入源を断つことを目的に科していたロシア産燃料に対する制裁を一時解除した。

WASHINGTON, Oct 16 : The FBI and the US cyber defense agency CISA are urging election officials - and the American public - to be on guard against AI-powered tricks ahead of next month's midterm elections.
Here are more details:
• An alert issued Friday by CISA and the FBI says that hackers may try to disrupt the midterm elections using bogus text messages and emails aimed at stealing passwords or other sensitive data.
• The alert says that "election officials, candidates, and their political organizations are attractive targets to malicious cyber criminals."
• The alert says that "super intelligence," a Trump-approved term for AI, is allowing hackers to sharpen their rogue emails and texts to make them look and sound more convincing.

WASHINGTON, Oct 16 : The FBI and the US cyber defense agency CISA are urging election officials - and the American public - to be on guard against AI-powered tricks ahead of next month's midterm elections.
Here are more details:
• An alert issued Friday by CISA and the FBI says that hackers may try to disrupt the midterm elections using bogus text messages and emails aimed at stealing passwords or other sensitive data.
• The alert says that "election officials, candidates, and their political organizations are attractive targets to malicious cyber criminals."
• The alert says that "super intelligence," a Trump-approved term for AI, is allowing hackers to sharpen their rogue emails and texts to make them look and sound more convincing.

Source: Reuters

items.title: アングル：ＡＩ投資ブームが資金争奪戦招く、中銀は高金利長期化警戒
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Francesco Canepa　Leika Kihara　Rae Wee

[バンコク １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Francesco Canepa　Leika Kihara　Rae Wee

[バンコク １６日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）の投資ブームが世界的な資金争奪戦を引き起こしている。各国の中央銀行幹部は、金利が高止まりし、政府は長年の財政大盤振る舞いの後に緊縮を迫られる未来を思い描かざるを得なくなっている。

半導体やデータセンターから電力網や通信網に至るまで、政府や企業はＡＩに直接・間接に関連するプロジェクトに資金をつぎ込んでおり、世界経済に勢いを与えると同時に、金利を押し上げている。

国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行の年次総会のためタイの首都バンコクに集結した主要国の中央銀行幹部は、ＡＩが約束する生産性向上よりはるかに先行して投資が殺到しているため、ブームは新たなインフレ圧力と金融リスクをも生み出していると指摘した。

ウォーシュ米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）議長は「中央銀行の立場であれば、これをショックとして認識せざるを得ない」と指摘。「供給サイドに影響が及ぶ前に、経済の需要サイドを明らかに直撃している」と認めた。

ウォーシュ氏は、米国は幅広い「投資の急増」の恩恵を受けていると説明する一方、最終的な勝者が依然不透明な、技術や投資家、企業、政策当局者のせめぎ合いの中で、移行過程は「非常に荒れたものになる」可能性があると警告した。

主要２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）の他の中銀幹部数人は、ＡＩ投資を支える明るい収益見通しがわずかに見直されるだけでも、今週のアジア市場で起きたハイテク株の売りが示したように、市場に深刻な動揺を引き起こしかねないと述べた。

＜雲に隠れた星＞

今回の議論は、世界的な貯蓄過剰と低過ぎるインフレが続くことを政策当局者が懸念していた、２００８年の金融危機後の数年間からの顕著な転換を示している。

今や中銀幹部は逆の問題、すなわち資本に対する需要が過剰であるという問題を一層強く認識している。

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのカザークス・ラトビア中銀総裁はロイターに「世界的な資金争奪戦が起きている。ＡＩ投資は資金コストを押し上げる主要因の一つだ」と語った。

米国から日本、ドイツに至るまで、政府が防衛、産業政策、エネルギー関連の事業で巨額の借り入れを行っていることが、こうした圧力を増幅させている。

中銀幹部にとっての含意は、経済を安定的に維持するために必要な金利水準、いわゆる自然利子率（ｒスター）が上昇している可能性があるということだ。

南アフリカ準備銀行（中央銀行）のクガニャゴ総裁は「現時点でｒスターを算出する上での問題は、星が雲に覆われており、しかもその雲が非常に厚いことだ」と述べ、「ｒスターがより高いことは分かっているが、どれほど高いのかは分からない」と語った。

中立金利が上昇すれば、同じ金利水準でも従来考えられていたほど景気抑制的ではないことを意味する。

イングランド銀行（中央銀行）のピル主席エコノミストは「平均すれば、金利はもう少し高くなるかもしれない」と述べた。

日銀はすでに、ＡＩ関連需要を最近の利上げの背景要因の一つとして挙げており、投資主導の物価圧力がより広範で持続的になっていると主張している。

エコノミストはイングランド銀が１１月５日の次回金融政策委員会で利上げすると予想している。ＥＣＢとＦＲＢは９月に利上げを実施し、両行とも１２月に再度利上げを行うと市場は織り込んでいる。

＜もはや安い資金はない＞

構造的に金利が上昇する見通しは、金利がゼロ近辺で推移していた期間に多額の債務を積み上げた政府にとって課題となる。国債利回りは世界的に上昇しており、ここ数週間で一部は世界金融危機前以来の水準に達した。

ユーロ圏、とりわけ巨額の債務を抱えるフランスが特にそのあおりを受けやすいとみられている。

ＡＩ主導の投資増加の多くは米国で発生しており、日本やアジアの他地域でもある程度生じている。一方、欧州側で明確な勝者と言える企業は、オランダの半導体製造装置大手ＡＳＭＬやドイツのシーメンスなど数社にとどまる。

さらにユーロ圏はイランやウクライナでの戦争に伴うエネルギーコストの上昇に直面しており、これがインフレ圧力を増大させ、財政を圧迫している。

ＥＣＢのラガルド総裁はバンコクでのＣＮＮのイベントで「一部の国がより大きな影響を受ける特別な事情がある。フランスがその一例だ」と述べ、「それについては、第一の、そして最大の解決策はフランス国内にあり、財政政策に関わるものだ」と語った。

items.title: Bank of Canada set for pair of important data drops ahead of 'live' rate decision
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: The Bank of Canada will get a raft of fresh data to start next week as it weighs what could be a pivotal interest rate decision at the end of the month.
items.body: The Bank of Canada will get a raft of fresh data to start next week as it weighs what could be a pivotal interest rate decision at the end of the month. Statistics Canada is set to release its September inflation data on Monday, giving the central bank a look at how energy price pressures are influencing other parts of the consumer basket. A Reuters poll of economists expects the annual rate of inflation rose to 3.2 per cent in September, up from three per cent in August, according to LSEG Data & Analytics. RBC assistant chief economist Nathan Janzen said he expects inflation held steady at three per cent last month. Persistently high gasoline prices tied to the ongoing war in Iran will remain the biggest fuel for inflation, he said. “We know that energy prices are high. What we don’t know yet is the extent that those higher energy prices have or are going to spill over to broader inflation pressures,” Janzen said. The Bank of Canada signalled at the start of the Middle East conflict last spring that it would look through a temporary rise in energy costs tied to the war. But officials have warned that the longer global oil prices remain high, the greater the risks that inflation spreads past the gas pump. In that case, the central bank could be forced to raise its policy rate, which has stood for nearly a year at 2.25 per cent. Most economists consider that level to be modestly stimulative to growth. Janzen said the Bank of Canada’s upcoming decision on Oct. 28 will be a “live” meeting, where the door is open for the central bank to raise its policy rate, but a hike is not his base case scenario. Even if the September price data shows signs inflationary pressures are spreading past the gas pumps, Janzen said the central bank will be weighing that against signs of softness in the labour market and wider economy. Statistics Canada reported last week that the economy shed 68,000 jobs in September, a second consecutive month of falling employment. A re-escalating trade dispute with the United States has also hampered growth prospects heading into the fourth quarter. “Higher energy prices — all else equal — would mean broader inflation pressures would be expected to rise in the future. But if the economy is getting weaker, then there are some offsetting disinflationary forces there as well,” Janzen said. “It puts (the Bank of Canada) still in a wait-and-see mode — very, very data dependent.” The Bank of Canada will also release its own quarterly surveys of businesses and consumers on Monday, which can give the bank a better sense of whether firms are planning to pass their own rising costs on to consumers. Janzen said inflation expectations and business confidence will help inform the central bank whether higher prices among producers could be passed on to store shelves in the months to come. --- Craig Lord, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 16, 2026.

FAST

Oct 16 : French media and digital regulator Arcom has opened an investigation into Mym, a France-based platform offering subscription-based content including adult material, over suspected breaches of the EU's Digital Services Act (DSA).
Arcom said on Friday it had sent Mym a formal request for information on October 14, giving the platform 15 days to respond or face sanctions, after a preliminary review raised concerns about child protection and service transparency.
Mym did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
• Arcom suspects Mym may have breached the DSA in two areas: protecting minors, including age-verification measures, and transparency requirements, citing incomplete terms of use and insufficient information about its recommendation systems

Worsening water crisis sparks protests in Mexico’s Guadalajara

By Cassandra Garrison
GUADALAJARA/MEXICO CITY, Oct 16 (Reuters) – Residents in Guadalajara, one of Mexico’s biggest cities, are demanding answers over a worsening water-quality crisis that has left many households reporting foul-smelling, sediment-filled tap water and sparked police clashes as protesters urge government action.

A major protest last weekend put the issue in the national spotlight after police deployed water cannons and tear gas, dozens of people were injured, and officials said nearly 40 people were arrested. The incident prompted President Claudia Sheinbaum to rebuke the police for their tough response and pledge to review two water infrastructure projects for the area. 

Still, further demonstrations are planned in the coming days as frustration builds, with videos circulating on social media of people collecting buckets and jars of murky brown or black water flowing from their taps. 

Show Full Article

The crisis has intensified scrutiny of water management across a metropolitan area of more than five million people that is also Mexico’s largest industrial and manufacturing center, located in the western state of Jalisco. The problems echo broader concerns across Mexico, where many major cities struggle with water quality and reliability amid aging infrastructure, pollution and mounting pressure on limited resources.

A June citizen-monitoring study by the Mexican Institute for Community Development (IMDEC) analyzed 184 household water samples from 90 neighborhoods and found that more than 93% contained no detectable residual chlorine, meaning much of the system lacked the disinfectant normally used to protect water from bacterial contamination. 

The study also reported elevated levels of lead, mercury, nitrates and E. coli, a bacterial indicator of fecal contamination, in some samples.

Following the findings, IMDEC called for a public-health alert, independent testing by accredited laboratories and investigations into the sources of contamination.

A spokesman for Jalisco’s government did not respond to a request for comment. 

At a rally on Thursday evening, Aleida Morales, 54, said that for at least 15 years, the water arriving at her home has often been cloudy and brown. The situation has helped drive residents into the streets, she said, because many feel economic development in Guadalajara, which was one of Mexico’s host cities for the World Cup this year, has come at the expense of environmental protection. 

Guadalajara sits within the larger Lerma-Santiago watershed, one of Mexico’s most polluted river systems and a region long burdened by wastewater, industrial pollution and rapid urban growth.

“There must be other, environmentally sustainable ways to create jobs,” Morales said. “The current approach is poisoning us.” 

Thirty years ago, her grandparents described some of the region’s local rivers and waterfalls as a “paradise.” 

“Today, they are the source of toxic contamination,” she added.  

LONG-STANDING ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES

Federal authorities have acknowledged broader environmental challenges affecting the region. 

In July, Sheinbaum and Secretary of Environment Alicia Barcena launched a 20 billion-peso ($1.09 billion) restoration program for the Lerma-Santiago basin and two other heavily polluted river systems, saying authorities had identified hundreds of priority pollution sources.

Allan Tejeda, an environmental engineering expert at the University of Guadalajara, said the crisis reflects years of accumulated pressures rather than a single contamination event.

He pointed to a combination of untreated or poorly treated wastewater, direct or undocumented discharges, rapid urban growth and chronic underinvestment in water infrastructure and treatment systems. 

Existing treatment facilities face growing pressure from contaminants entering the system and are increasingly inadequate for the scale of the challenge confronting the region, he said. 

“These issues have never received the attention they require,” Tejeda said.

The National Assembly for Water, Life, and Territory, a Mexican rights coalition, expressed solidarity with protesters in Jalisco and called for “a real, comprehensive and verifiable solution” to Guadalajara’s water crisis.

“Water is not a concession granted by governments nor a privilege reserved for those who can afford to pay for it,” the group said. “It is indispensable for life, health, food, work and the survival of our communities.”

($1 = 18.4010 Mexican pesos)

(Reporting by Cassandra Garrison in Mexico City; additonal reporting by José Luis Osorio in Guadalajara; Editing by Nia Williams)

items.title: Los votantes brasileños necesitan un debate entre Lula y Bolsonaro
items.author: Juan Pablo Spinetto
items.summary: Los votantes brasileños necesitan un debate cara a cara entre Lula y Bolsonaro. El drama del debate en Brasil llega a los mercados de apuestas; aumentan las apuestas a que Lula y Bolsonaro debatirán ...
items.body: Es la mayor contienda electoral del mundo este año, y sin embargo, todavía no hemos visto a los contendientes enfrentarse cara a cara. A tan solo 10 días de la crucial segunda vuelta del 25 de octubre, la celebración de los debates presidenciales de Brasil entre el presidente en funciones, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, y su rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, sigue siendo sorprendentemente incierta. En teoría, ambos candidatos ya han confirmado su participación en el primero de los dos debates televisados programados para el 18 y el 23 de octubre. Sin embargo, dos debates anteriores fueron cancelados: uno a última hora, justo antes de la primera vuelta, y otro que debía celebrarse el fin de semana pasado, oficialmente debido a un “conflicto de agenda“. El cálculo electoral cínico, el temor a errores no forzados y la animosidad mutua han impedido que las campañas concreten un debate hasta ahora. El miércoles, Kalshi le daba un 93% de probabilidades de que se produjera al menos un enfrentamiento, un aumento respecto al 63% del día anterior, después de que Bolsonaro cambiara de opinión y anunciara su asistencia al evento del domingo. El hecho de que exista un mercado de apuestas sobre si los candidatos debatirán da una idea de lo inestable que continúa siendo la situación. Lula, que está 5,6 puntos porcentuales por detrás de Bolsonaro en votos válidos según AtlasIntel/Bloomberg, tiene poco que perder y todas las razones para subirse al podio. Solo esperemos que, al final, este enfrentamiento tan esperado se produzca. De lo contrario, significaría un claro retroceso democrático en un país donde el apoyo a la democracia se está erosionando. Según la más reciente encuesta del Latinobarómetro, apenas el 41% de los brasileños afirma que la democracia es preferible a cualquier otra forma de gobierno, la cifra más baja de la región, solo por detrás de Guatemala. Los debates raramente cambian el rumbo de la campaña, aunque una reciente encuesta de Datafolha reveló que el 78% de los brasileños considera muy importante que Lula y Bolsonaro participen en ellos. Y si no lo hacen como ejercicio democrático, al menos deberían hacerlo por razones tácticas: desde Andrés Manuel López Obrador en 2006 hasta el propio Lula a inicios de este mes, los candidatos que han evitado los debates para proteger una ventaja imaginaria han pagado las consecuencias en las urnas posteriormente. Ante todo, Brasil necesita estos debates porque los votantes tienen derecho a escuchar, alto y claro, las propuestas concretas de los candidatos sobre tres de sus mayores preocupaciones: el cada vez mayor déficit fiscal, la crisis política en torno al Tribunal Supremo y la preocupante ola de inseguridad que azota al país. Cabe señalar que, hasta ahora, tanto Lula como Bolsonaro se han mostrado reacios a dar detalles sobre cómo abordarían estos problemas, convirtiendo la campaña más en una disputa verbal entre izquierda y derecha que en un intercambio serio de ideas. Por ejemplo, Bolsonaro ha dicho que, de ser elegido, aplicará una drástica reducción de impuestos, burocracia y corrupción para sanear el presupuesto, al estilo de Javier Milei en Argentina. No obstante, ha evitado precisar la cifra del ajuste fiscal. Si bien la prensa local ha informado que sus asesores económicos estudian un recorte presupuestario inicial de alrededor del 2% del PIB, públicamente han descartado privatizaciones, prometido fortalecer los programas sociales y anunciado recortes de impuestos a las empresas. El argumento de que el ajuste fiscal de Bolsonaro se centrará en los “excesos del gobierno” puede parecer razonable, pero no hace falta ser economista para saber que los cambios superficiales difícilmente lograrán que la deuda brasileña vuelva a un rumbo sostenible. Lula, por su parte, reforzó su mensaje contra el crimen tras su derrota en la primera vuelta, con una promesa renovada de encarcelar a los delincuentes: “Para los trabajadores, protección. Para los criminales, prisión”, es su nuevo lema. No sería descabellado preguntarse por qué él o su partido no han hecho esto durante los 16 años que llevan en el gobierno este siglo. Y luego está el espinoso tema del Tribunal Supremo, donde Lula se debate entre pedir una reforma del poder judicial y defender al controvertido juez Alexandre de Moraes, a quien Bolsonaro quiere destituir. Quien gane la segunda vuelta tendrá la potestad de nombrar al menos a cuatro magistrados del Tribunal Supremo durante el próximo mandato presidencial. Los brasileños merecen escuchar explícitamente de ambos candidatos qué cambios están considerando para mejorar una institución que ha perjudicado al país durante demasiado tiempo. Aunque se piense que el giro a la derecha de Brasil es, a estas alturas, imparable, los debates aportarían mayor transparencia sobre todos estos temas clave antes del día de las elecciones. Lamentablemente, los candidatos parecen más centrados en intentar obtener ventajas legales mediante fallos judiciales favorables que en ser completamente transparentes con los votantes. Efectivamente, un informe del medio local O Globo reveló que las campañas abrieron 698 casos contra sus rivales en los tribunales electorales solo durante la primera vuelta, casi tres veces más que en las elecciones anteriores. La gran mayoría de los casos fueron presentados por los representantes de Bolsonaro contra los de Lula, o viceversa. Esta estrategia implica un enorme derroche de recursos y de energía, y además es cobarde. En vez de perder el tiempo en disputas judiciales sin importancia, los candidatos deberían explicar al electorado qué van a hacer para mejorar sus vidas. Quien no sea capaz de enfrentarse a su rival más directo durante un par de horas para defender sus ideas, quizá debería plantearse dedicarse a otra cosa. Esta nota no refleja necesariamente la opinión del consejo editorial de Bloomberg LP y sus propietarios. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Colombia perdió 686.000 empleos en agosto y el desempleo alcanzó su nivel más alto en dos años
items.author: Daniel Guerrero
items.summary: El terremoto, la apreciación del peso y los mayores costos laborales y de producción presionaron el mercado laboral. La industria manufacturera fue el sector más afectado.
items.body: Bogotá — Colombia registró en agosto una de las señales más preocupantes para su mercado laboral desde la pandemia: la destrucción mensual de 686.000 puestos de trabajo, mientras la tasa de desempleo ajustada por estacionalidad subió a 9,7%, su nivel más alto en dos años, según un informe de Investigaciones Económicas del Banco de Bogotá, publicado el 15 de octubre. El deterioro se produjo después de que el mercado laboral mostrara señales de debilidad en julio. En agosto, la tasa de ocupación ajustada por estacionalidad cayó de 59% a 57,3%, reflejando una reducción en la proporción de personas ocupadas frente a la población en edad de trabajar. El informe advierte que la situación podría ser más grave de lo que refleja la cifra oficial de desempleo. La razón está en que una parte importante de las personas que perdieron su ocupación dejó de buscar trabajo y pasó a la inactividad. “Si la participación laboral se hubiera mantenido estable frente a julio, la tasa de desempleo habría ascendido hasta 11,0% y no a 9,7%”, señala el análisis de Investigaciones Económicas del Banco de Bogotá. Aunque el terremoto que afectó al país contribuyó al deterioro de la ocupación en varias regiones, el análisis identifica dificultades estructurales en diferentes actividades económicas como otro factor determinante. Entre agosto de 2025 y agosto de 2026, la industria manufacturera perdió 240.000 puestos de trabajo, la mayor reducción entre los sectores analizados. El entretenimiento y otras actividades registraron una caída de 102.000 empleos, mientras que la agricultura perdió 91.000. También disminuyó el número de ocupados en las actividades inmobiliarias, con 31.000 puestos menos; el sector financiero, con 27.000, y alojamiento y servicios de comida, con 17.000. En contraste, el comercio sumó 150.000 ocupados frente al año anterior, la construcción agregó 80.000 y los servicios sociales aumentaron en 96.000. El informe destaca que la pérdida de dinamismo en sectores productivos tradicionales plantea riesgos para la generación de empleo, especialmente en actividades que enfrentan mayores costos o dificultades de competitividad. Uno de los factores identificados por el Banco de Bogotá es la apreciación del peso colombiano , que ha reducido la competitividad de la industria manufacturera. Según el documento, esta actividad acumuló un crecimiento de apenas 1% en lo corrido de 2026, explicado en gran medida por la elaboración de bebidas y la refinación de petróleo, actividades que tienen una menor intensidad laboral. El turismo también muestra señales de debilitamiento. Entre abril y julio, la llegada de extranjeros pasó de 1,5 millones en 2025 a 1,4 millones en 2026, una disminución de 7,7%. Esta reducción afecta la actividad de alojamiento y los servicios de comida, sectores cuya capacidad para generar empleo depende, entre otros factores, del comportamiento de la demanda turística. El entretenimiento, por su parte, enfrenta una menor demanda ante el aumento de precios asociado al ajuste del salario mínimo, según el análisis. En el sector agrícola, la presión proviene del incremento de los precios internacionales de los fertilizantes y de la llegada del fenómeno de El Niño, factores que elevan los costos de producción. “En conjunto, estos factores han terminado reflejándose en una menor capacidad de generación de empleo”, plantea el informe. El comportamiento regional también sugiere que el sismo no fue el único responsable de la caída de la ocupación. Pereira, una de las ciudades más afectadas por el terremoto, registró la mayor destrucción de empleo frente a su nivel de hace 12 meses. Sin embargo, la segunda mayor caída se presentó en Santa Marta, donde las afectaciones por el evento fueron limitadas. A su vez, mientras Quibdó y Manizales registraron reducciones en la ocupación, Cali, Armenia y Popayán mostraron aumentos. Para los investigadores, estas diferencias apuntan a la presencia de factores estructurales que van más allá de los efectos inmediatos del desastre natural. En el agregado nacional, las cifras ajustadas por estacionalidad muestran que el número de ocupados pasó de 24,3 millones en julio a 23,6 millones en agosto. Al mismo tiempo, la población desempleada aumentó de 2,2 millones a 2,5 millones y la población inactiva pasó de 14,7 millones a 15,1 millones. El aumento de la inactividad ayuda a explicar por qué la tasa de desempleo no refleja por completo la magnitud de la pérdida de ocupaciones. Las perspectivas del mercado laboral también enfrentan riesgos asociados con la moderación del empleo público, las altas tasas de interés, el ajuste fiscal y los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño. El Banco de Bogotá advierte que la pérdida de dinamismo de sectores productivos clave, sumada a la moderación del empleo público, plantea desafíos para sostener los resultados del mercado laboral en los próximos meses. En sus proyecciones, Investigaciones Económicas estima que la tasa de desempleo promedio en las 13 principales ciudades del país se ubicará en 8,8% en 2026 y aumentará a 9,4% en 2027. Estas cifras corresponden a promedios anuales para las 13 ciudades y no deben confundirse con la tasa nacional observada en agosto, que fue de 9,4%, o con la tasa nacional ajustada por estacionalidad, que alcanzó 9,7%.

items.title: CDC reports 4,410 measles cases as outbreak grows
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The US CDC on Friday reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15, an increase of 330 from its last update a week ago, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues.
items.body:
The US CDC on Friday reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15, an increase of 330 from its last update a week ago, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues.
Here are key details:
Measles-related hospitalizations this year stand at 451, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said
The state of Pennsylvania has reported five measles-related deaths
The CDC has confirmed [USN:L4N45L13A TEXT:"two measles-associated deaths"] in 2026, though it has not identified the states involved
Pennsylvania has reported 1,260 measles cases this year as of October 16, with 238 disease-related hospitalizations, according to state health department data
Last month, the CDC [USN:L4N45A17G TEXT:"shifted"] to using mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics for measles-related deaths, rather than relying on state health departments, a change that has drawn scrutiny
The CDC [USN:L4N45Z1Q3 TEXT:"said"] on Tuesday it would deploy more support to Pennsylvania to help investigate the outbreak
Children and teenagers aged 5 to 19 were the largest group affected by the disease at 1,856, or 42% of cases, followed by adults aged 20 and older at 1,787 cases, or 41%, CDC data showed
Earlier this month, the state of New York [USN:L4N45R1BM TEXT:"declared"] a disaster emergency for the measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a US state

items.title: Zubimendi close to Arsenal return, Hincapie still sidelined, says Arteta
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said Martin Zubimendi could return for Sunday's Premier League match against Nottingham Forest, but Piero Hincapie is expected to remain sidelined after both players picked up injuries last week.
items.body:
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said Martin Zubimendi could return for Sunday's Premier League match against Nottingham Forest, but Piero Hincapie is expected to remain sidelined after both players picked up injuries last week.
The duo suffered ankle injuries during a training session following Arsenal's 2-1 win over Leeds United and were ruled out of Tuesday's Champions League victory over Lille
“Piero (Hincapie) is evolving really well... I am sure it's not going to take long, but he will probably need another week or two," Arteta told reporters on Friday
“Zubimendi looks much better... We have another session tomorrow, and after that we will assess whether he's available to play against Forest”
Arsenal will also be without Christos Tzolis, who is recovering from a muscle injury sustained on international duty, and William Saliba, who remains sidelined with a back problem
