Oct 16 : Michael Saylor's Strategy faces potential removal from MSCI's global equity indexes under new rules adopted on Thursday, threatening billions of dollars in passive investment in the bitcoin buyer.
Shares of Strategy, the world's biggest corporate bitcoin holder and a constituent of the MSCI USA and MSCI World indexes, fell 4.2 per cent on Friday.
MSCI said on Thursday non-operating companies will be ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30, as part of its November index review. It will publish the final list of affected companies on November 11.
The decision follows a review MSCI began a year ago, when it proposed excluding digital asset treasury companies on the grounds that they resemble investment funds, which are already barred from its indexes. MSCI deferred that plan in January and opened a broader review on all non-operating companies.

MSCI defines non-operating companies as investment funds and business development companies, and other companies whose finances make them look like one.
Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet are on MSCI's list of potential deletions. SharpLink and several other crypto treasury companies are on a watchlist for possible removal.
The changes are aimed at expanding MSCI’s exclusions for passive investment vehicles, with companies required to meet financial tests on their operating assets to remain eligible.
Index inclusion matters to companies such as Strategy because passive funds and other investors tracking benchmarks are required to hold their shares.
Strategy did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The company warned last year that an exclusion would result in $2.8 billion of its stock being liquidated and would "chill" the industry.
Strategy, which pioneered the model of raising money through stock and debt sales to buy bitcoin, had a market value of about $64.3 billion on Friday. Its shares were down 4.8 per cent in 2026.

FAST

NEW YORK/PARIS, Oct 16 : Global stocks edged lower on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.
Markets have been rattled this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks.
Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after stronger-than-expected inflation data on Wednesday, while investors piled into Treasuries and other government bonds.
On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were trading down and were headed for weekly losses. The Dow was flat but set for a weekly gain.

Technology and communication services were driving losses while top gainers were utilities and consumer staples stocks.
CoreWeave's shares shed 9 per cent on the day and were on track to lose nearly 23 per cent this week amid increasing investor scrutiny of the financing for the massive AI infrastructure buildout.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.01 per cent, the S&P 500 fell 0.61 per cent, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.3 per cent.  
The MSCI World Equity Index lost 0.10 per cent and was set for a weekly loss. European stock indexes, hit less hard by Thursday's selloff, were higher, with the STOXX 600 up 0.67 per cent. London's FTSE 100 rose 0.38 per cent.
"We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund, said.
"Our view is that there's going to be some really significant winners. But you have to be careful on the financing capability because companies don't get into trouble because their assets don't exceed their liabilities. They get into trouble when they have liquidity issues."
Asian stocks mostly rose and bond markets steadied on Friday, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves. 
Indonesian equities suffered their biggest drop since 1998 after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging-market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds. 
DOLLAR FALLS, BONDS RECOVER
The dollar index fell 0.23 per cent and was on track for its first weekly decline after four weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, analysts said.
The euro rose from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.10 per cent at $1.1232.
The Japanese yen strengthened 0.04 per cent against the greenback to 157.92 per dollar. 
European government bond yields edged higher, while US bond yields fell. Germany's 10-year yield rose 0.14 basis point to 3.411 per cent. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 0.17 basis points to 5.085 per cent.
Even so, yields have eased this week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May.
Brent crude futures rose 0.85 per cent to $106.83 a barrel and were headed for a second straight weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have surged in the past 10 days.
Gold gained support from the weaker dollar, rising 0.17 per cent to about $4,177.14 an ounce.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Swiss journalist risks court sentence for exposing top banker
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Zurich prosecutors this week charged Swiss journalist Lukas Haessig with violating banking secrecy over reporting that set off a high-profile corporate criminal trial of the former boss of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, Haessig said on his financial blog Inside Paradeplatz.
items.body:
Zurich prosecutors this week charged Swiss journalist Lukas Haessig with violating banking secrecy over reporting that set off a high-profile corporate criminal trial of the former boss of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, Haessig said on his financial blog Inside Paradeplatz.
Zurich-based Inside Paradeplatz published a series of articles in 2016 about Pierin Vincenz, former CEO of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, and his business partner Beat Stocker, who were found guilty of fraud in April 2022
That verdict [USN:L8N4422LC TEXT:"is currently under review"] by a higher court expected to rule in January 2027
Police in June 2025 searched the blog's Zurich office and home of its founder, seizing evidence linked to suspected violation of Swiss banking law
Prosecutors had dropped the case in December 2025, but Zurich's High Court in April said a court must decide how the banking secrecy provision should be interpreted after a complaint by Stocker
Article 47 of the Swiss Banking Act criminalises disclosure of confidential information leaked by bank insiders, with penalties of up to three years in prison or a fine
Press freedom group Reporters Without Borders Switzerland called the charges troubling and said Article 47 of the Swiss banking act must not be used to prosecute journalists
Inside Paradeplatz's reporting was clearly in the public interest, Reporters Without Borders said, adding the banking secrecy law had a chilling effect and pointing to "legal shortcomings" in Switzerland on press freedom
Prosecutors said the presumption of innocence applies to Haessig. No court date has yet been set

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [東京 １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[東京 １６日 ロイター] - トヨタ自動車は、２０３０年までに世界で販売する全５０車種を「ソフトウエア定義車両（ＳＤＶ）」にする。独自のソフトウェアプラットフォーム（基盤）「Ａｒｅｎｅ（アリーン）」を新車に順次搭載する。ＳＤＶで先行する中国や米国の電気自動車（ＥＶ）メーカーを追撃し、年間１０００万台規模の新車販売に加え、売った後もソフトの更新などを通じて課金するビジネスモデルを強化する。

同社広報によると、中嶋裕樹副社長が先週、アリーンの導入計画をベルギーのブリュッセルで投資家に説明。３５年にはトヨタ車以外にも展開し、提携先など他社の車両にアリーンを供給する考えも明らかにしたという。

トヨタは２５年に発売したスポーツ多目的車（ＳＵＶ）「ＲＡＶ４」で初めてアリーンを導入し、今後販売する新車に順次展開する方針を示唆していた。

ＳＤＶは、スマートフォンのように購入後も無線通信を通じてソフトを更新し、先進運転支援技術やエンタテイメントなど車の性能や機能を向上させる車で、米テスラや中国勢が先行している。

items.title: UK's FTSE 100 logs strongest week in six months on defensive-sector rally
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Britain's blue-chip stocks had their best week in six months, as investors flocking to defensive sectors offset a rout in AI-linked stocks, while finance minister John Healey's reassurances on fiscal discipline also helped risk appetite.
items.body:
Britain's blue-chip stocks had their best week in six months, as investors flocking to defensive sectors offset a rout in AI-linked stocks, while finance minister John Healey's reassurances on fiscal discipline also helped risk appetite.
The export-heavy FTSE 100 (.FTSE) closed 0.38% higher at 10,881.90 points, logging a weekly gain of 3.1%, the biggest since early April, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) gained 0.45%.
UK's large-cap ETFs attracted $3.38 billion in estimated net inflows year to date, already the biggest annual total since 2020, data from Morningstar showed
"Flows into passive funds typically follow performance, but they also reflect investors looking to diversify away from US mega-cap technology and broaden their equity exposure," said Michael Born, an analyst at Morningstar
Consumer staples supported gains. Cigarette maker British American Tobacco (BATS.L) rose 2.1%, while Johnnie Walker owner Diageo (DGE.L) gained 1.9%
The beverages (.FTNMX451010) and medical equipment and services (.FTNMX201020) sectors advanced 7.8% and 6.9%, respectively, in the week
Homebuilders (.FTNMX402020) jumped over 6% in the week after Healey [USN:S8N4040BJ TEXT:"reaffirmed"] his commitment to fiscal discipline on Thursday
Banks (.FTNMX301010) were muted on Friday, recovering from early losses triggered by a [USN:SPN46001Q TEXT:"report"] that Healey was likely to tax the lenders in the budget
Bank of England [USN:L1N46202H TEXT:"Governor Andrew Bailey"] said signs of second-round inflation were limited ahead of next week's inflation data
Traders are pricing in four BoE rate hikes over the next 12 months, according to LSEG data
Defence stocks (.FTNMX502010) extended a strong run on the day: BAE Systems (BAES.L) and Babcock International (BAB.L) rose 2.6% and 3.6%, respectively
THG (THG.L) had its best week in six months, surging 30% after the e-commerce firm raised its annual adjusted core profit forecast on Thursday

items.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for steep weekly losses as AI jitters rattle investors
items.author: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
items.creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
items.summary: The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses.
items.body:
The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses.
The S&P 500 information technology index (.SPLRCT) fell 1.5% and was the biggest drag. [USN:L6N4620IB TEXT:"Nvidia-backed"] CoreWeave (CRWV.O) slid 10.3% on lingering debt concerns. The data centre operator's bonds sold off sharply this week, pushing yields to above 15%.
Semiconductors bore the brunt of the selloff, with the broader chips index (.SOX) dropping 1.8% — set for its steepest eight-session percentage decline since the "Liberation Day" selloff in April 2025.
Most megacap stocks tumbled and brought the Nasdaq close to a one-month low. Meta (META.O) slipped 2.3% and Microsoft (MSFT.O) lost 1.8%.
AI stocks have cratered this week over concerns that data centre operators might not turn profitable in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. Worries over rising competition from China also dented sentiment.
"When investors start worrying that AI names are overvalued, they gravitate toward lower-multiple stocks with stable cash flows," said Dennis Dick, founder and market structure analyst at Triple D Trading.
Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611DN TEXT:"are weighing a lower valuation"] for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
At 12:19 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 14.74 points, or 0.03%, to 52,162.95, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 43.53 points, or 0.56%, to 7,700.38 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 348.31 points, or 1.30%, to 26,364.72.
Most other S&P 500 sectors rose. The energy index (.SPNY) was the biggest percentage gainer, up 1.5%, while the financials index (.SPSY) rose 1%.
Gains in Goldman Sachs (GS.N) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) lifted the Dow to its highest level in over a month. The index is set for a weekly advance, with investors rushing to defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples.
"What we're seeing now is money rotating out of a very crowded AI trade and into value names," Dick added.
The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since early June, faced with an AI-led rout, mixed bank earnings and inflation data. The Nasdaq eyed its sharpest weekly fall since June 22.
Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week have confirmed that price pressures are extending beyond energy products.
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh also said a spending surge was boosting inflation, but added that the US [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"economy"] remained resilient and benefited from the AI-driven investment boom.
Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays [USN:FWN4622T4 TEXT:"now expects"] 25 basis point hikes each in December and January.
Meanwhile, Tesla (TSLA.O) failed to hold on to gains from before the bell — as much as 3% — after unveiling a [USN:L1N46200L TEXT:"redesigned Roadster"], powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX.
Netflix (NFLX.O) [USN:L4N46128P TEXT:"appointed"] former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.6%.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.94-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and no new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 200 new lows.

items.title: France, Germany strike deal on car emissions and UK special status
items.author: Philip Blenkinsop
items.creator: Philip Blenkinsop
items.summary: France and Germany struck a deal on Friday to soften proposed EU car emissions rules and open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the bloc's Made in EU rules.
items.body:
France and Germany struck a deal on Friday to soften proposed EU car emissions rules and open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the bloc's [USN:L6N45E0Q1 TEXT:""Made in EU" rules"].
The European Commission [USN:L6N3XM0EA TEXT:"proposed last year"] that automakers cut CO2 emissions by 90% from 2021 levels in 2035, with the remaining 10% offset through measures such as the use of low-carbon steel and alternative fuels.
Under the Franco-German plan, the 2035 target would be set at 90%, but without the need for additional compensatory measures. The approach is broadly in line with the wishes of German automakers.
European automotive stocks gained after the deal was announced, lifting the STOXX 600 Automobile and Parts Index (.SXAP) nearly 2%.
The joint plan also addresses an EU proposal introducing local-content and low-carbon requirements for products bought through public procurement, public auctions or subsidy schemes.
France has pushed for these products to be limited to those manufactured in the European Union. Other EU members, including Germany, argue that countries closely linked to EU automotive supply chains and free-trade-agreement partners should also be included.
The Franco-German plan says that for the automotive sector, "Made in EU" should cover the EU's 27 countries and other European partners that were part of the EU internal market on January 1, 2020.
That would include Britain, which left the EU single market at the end of 2020.
Volkswagen , Europe's largest automaker, said the compromise would help the industry contribute "to climate protection without jeopardizing its competitiveness."
The German company said the "Made in EU" proposals "provide a clear incentive for production and investment in Europe".
An official at British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's Downing Street office said inclusion in the "Made in EU" scheme would boost Britain's automotive sector. However, he said the Franco-German proposal requires wider European backing and that details had yet to be seen.
The Franco-German plan also says that inclusion should be subject to an agreement on full reciprocity, along with "dynamic alignment with EU conditions for investment from third countries and with EU trade protection measures".
That could mean Britain adopting measures the EU has taken to [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"restrict imports"] of Chinese-built hybrid and battery-electric vehicles.
Speaking to reporters in London, Renault (RENA.PA) CEO Francois Provost said "obviously, the UK should be part of" the "Made in the EU" scheme as it is part of Europe's automotive "ecosystem."
But he said Britain should in turn ditch its [USN:L8N446056 TEXT:"EV sales mandate"] and adopt the same rules as the EU.
"The two automotive industrial policies should be consistent," Provost said.
A GOOD DAY FOR JOBS OR A 'HISTORIC MISTAKE'? The Franco-German paper also proposed compliance periods spanning multiple years for CO2 emission targets, no revision before 2030 of the utility factor for hybrid vehicles, which measures the share of driving done electrically, and recognition of cars powered by renewable and low-carbon fuels as zero-emission vehicles.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the deal "a good day for motorists and for jobs in Germany, France and Europe", adding that Italy largely agreed with the proposals.
The deal will not please all automakers. Toyota's (7203.T) European division, which sells cars in Europe from plants in the EU, Britain, Turkey and Japan, said on Thursday that including partners such as Britain, Canada, Japan, South Korea and Turkey would give the EU the scale needed to compete with China.
[USN:L1N45Z0LF TEXT:"Turkey's trade minister"] said this week on a trip to Brussels that trusted partners like Turkey should not be excluded.
Green and environmental groups criticised the emissions proposals.
German Greens lawmaker Swantje Michaelsen said Germany's government was holding back the industry as high fuel prices accelerate EV demand.
Anna Krajinska of transport and environment campaign group T&E called the deal a "historic mistake" that would reduce the incentive for automakers to invest in EVs.
"German and French political leaders claim they are acting to save jobs, but this may well be the deal that buries Europe’s auto industry," she said.
France and Germany must convince other EU members and the European Parliament for their plans to enter into force. They are unlikely to reach a final common text before early next year, after an EU-UK summit planned for November 20.

items.title: El cobre impulsa al alza el complejo metalero antes de la LME Week
items.author: Polina Devitt
items.creator: Polina Devitt
items.summary: Los precios del cobre impulsaron al alza a otros metales básicos el viernes, gracias al apoyo que supuso la debilidad del dólar, mientras que los mercados bursátiles se estabilizaban tras la fuerte caída del jueves en los valores tecnológicos, mejorando el apetito por el riesgo por los metales dependientes del crecimiento.
items.body:
Los precios del cobre impulsaron al alza a otros metales básicos el viernes, gracias al apoyo que supuso la debilidad del dólar, mientras que los mercados bursátiles se estabilizaban tras la fuerte caída del jueves en los valores tecnológicos, mejorando el apetito por el riesgo por los metales dependientes del crecimiento.
* A las 1600 GMT, el contrato de referencia del cobre a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) ganó un 0,3%, a 14.384 dólares por tonelada, recuperándose del mínimo de casi dos semanas de 14.256 dólares alcanzado el jueves.
* La reunión anual LME Week, que se celebrará la próxima semana en Londres y a la que acuden consumidores, productores, operadores y corredores del sector de los metales, coincide con el tercer miércoles del mes, fecha en la que vencen los contratos mensuales de la LME.
* El cobre y el zinc, junto con el aluminio y el estaño, se encaminan hacia la próxima semana en situación de "backwardation", con los contratos al contado cotizando con una prima respecto a los contratos a tres meses, una estructura que apunta a cierta escasez en la oferta a corto plazo.
* "La verdadera escasez de cobre refinado este año se ha debido a que el metal refinado ha seguido inundando el mercado estadounidense ante la perspectiva de los aranceles previstos para enero del año que viene", afirmó Ian Roper, investigador de metales de la correduría Marex, en una presentación.
* Sin embargo, Roper prevé que el cobre se vea sometido a presión de cara a fines de año, ya que a principios de diciembre comienza a cerrarse el plazo para que los envíos pasen la aduana estadounidense antes de que termine el año, lo que liberará parte del metal para los mercados fuera de Estados Unidos.
* El cobre acumula un alza del 16% en lo que va de año, tras tocar un máximo histórico de 14.875 dólares hace cinco semanas.
* Entre otros metales básicos de la LME, el aluminio subió un 0,5%, a 3.001 dólares por tonelada; el zinc ganó un 0,7%, a 3.690,5 dólares; el níquel avanzó un 0,7%, a 15.325 dólares; el plomo mejoró un 0,4%, a 1.887 dólares; y el estaño sumó un 0,3%, a 50.240 dólares.

Oct 16 : Alphabet's Waymo said on Friday it plans to bring its autonomous ride-hailing service to Toronto in 2028, marking the self-driving company's first planned deployment in Canada and its latest move to expand beyond the US.
Here are some details:
• Waymo, which operates commercial robotaxi services in several US cities, said it would partner with Element Fleet Management for fleet operations in Toronto as it expands to markets including London and Tokyo
• The company said it will begin groundwork in Canada's largest city, including mapping and engagement with local authorities, as it prepares for a future deployment of the Waymo Driver.
• Waymo also plans to create hundreds of jobs over time in fleet maintenance, validation driving, customer service and other operations functions

AMSTERDAM, Oct 16 : Shares in computer chip packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) fell 3 per cent on Friday after influential semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis reported that one of the company's main growth products will face competition from bigger rival ASML.
The SemiAnalysis report analysed 27 patent filings by ASML, which it said indicated ASML was developing a hybrid bonding product.
Besi is a fraction of the size of ASML, the biggest maker of equipment used to make semiconductors, but Besi is a leader in hybrid bonding, an advanced packaging technology being used to create a new generation of more powerful three-dimensional chips.  
ASML has not confirmed it is developing such a tool. Besi did not respond to requests for comment.

Besi shares were down 3 per cent at €158.50, while ASML was up 1.1 per cent at €1,480 in midday Amsterdam trading.
A spokesperson for ASML declined to comment on the SemiAnalysis report but pointed to the company's launch of its first advanced packaging tool last year. "We continue to look at which directions the 3D integration industry will evolve ... and where ASML's expertise can be of additional value," the company said in a statement at that time.
In March, Reuters reported that ASML was planning additional packaging tools, citing Chief Technical Officer Marco Pieters in an interview.
"The semiconductor market has already signalled that packaging is one of those next frontiers where performance gains can be unlocked, and ASML seems to be building next-gen tools headed in the same direction," said Nick Rossolillo, co-founder of Chip Stock Investor.
"We see the new batch of packaging tools, beyond an EUV pipeline, as critical to pulling off the growth needed to justify (ASML's) elevated valuation."

items.title: イスラエル人入植者、ヨルダン川西岸でオリーブ収穫中の村人襲撃
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Pesha Magid

[アブファラ（ヨルダン川西岸） １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Pesha Magid

[アブファラ（ヨルダン川西岸） １６日 ロイター] - 覆面をしたイスラエル人入植者数十人が１６日、パレスチナ自治区ヨルダン川西岸の村でオリーブを収穫していた村人を組織的に襲撃し、木を焼いたり、石を投げたりした。記者を含む少なくとも２人が負傷した。

現場を目撃したロイター記者によると、オリーブの実を摘むためにアブファラの村人が畑に集まっていたところ、入植者約８０人が畑を見下ろす丘から下りてきた。一部は投石器を使い、村人たちに向けて石を放ったという。

襲撃のさなか、イスラエル軍のジープ少なくとも２台が土ぼこりを上げながら現場一帯を走行した。軍の到着後も襲撃は続き、イスラエル兵はジープを避けて逃げたパレスチナ人に向けて催涙ガスを発射した。

現場では実弾の発砲音が聞こえた。ロイターの写真記者は武装した入植者少なくとも１人が銃を撃つのを目撃した。

イスラエル軍はコメント要請に応じていない。

パレスチナの医療関係者によると、２人が負傷し、ラマラ周辺の病院に搬送された。うち１人は米紙ワシントン・ポストの写真記者だった。

アブファラでの襲撃に先立ち、１６日朝にはトゥルムスアヤ村周辺でも同様の襲撃があった。入植者らはオリーブを収穫していた農家の集団を襲い、車３台に火を付けた。

イスラエルの入植活動を監視する人権団体「イェシュ・ディン」によると、占領下のヨルダン川西岸では、イスラエル人入植者によるパレスチナ人への暴力が急増している。オリーブ収穫が始まった頃にあたる９月２７日以降、少なくとも１７０件の襲撃が起きた。

ネタニヤフ首相は暴力を批判しているが、取り締まりに向けた措置はほとんど講じていない。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Chen Aizhu

[シンガポール １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Chen Aizhu

[シンガポール １６日 ロイター] - 中国石油天然気（ペトロチャイナ）で、原油などの取引を手掛けるトレーディング部門の２０２６年の利益が過去最高を更新する見通しであることが、複数の関係者の話で分かった。イラン紛争によって中東産原油の売買形態が一変し、需給が逼迫する中、中国国外の製油所の利幅が大幅に拡大している。

アジア最大の石油・天然ガス生産会社で中国第２位の石油精製会社であるペトロチャイナは、大規模な生産・供給ポートフォリオと広範な精製・小売りネットワークを生かして利益を上げ、戦争に伴う供給混乱の影響を回避できている。

事情に詳しい関係者２人によると、ペトロチャイナのトレーディング部門、中国石油国際事業（ＰＣＩ）の２６年粗利益は２００億元（３０億ドル）を超え過去最高になる見込み。

同部門の幹部によると、通常、ＰＣＩ部門利益の半分以上を稼ぎ出す原油部門の利益が１０月初旬までに、２５年通年の２倍以上に達したほか、石油製品部門や天然ガス部門も好調に推移している。

同社は決算でトレーディング部門利益の内訳を開示していない。８月に発表した上半期グループ純利益は約１４６億５０００万ドルだった。

items.title: Trudy forecast to near Mexico's Pacific coast as major hurricane through the weekend
items.author: Aida Pelaez-fernandez
items.creator: Aida Pelaez-fernandez
items.summary: Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified on Friday, carrying maximum winds near 120 mph (195 kph), and is expected to approach Mexico's Pacific coast as a major storm during the weekend.
items.body:
Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified on Friday, carrying maximum winds near 120 mph (195 kph), and is expected to approach Mexico's Pacific coast as a major storm during the weekend.
Additional strengthening is still forecast before Trudy nears the coast of Jalisco and Colima states late on Saturday as a life-threatening major hurricane, Mexican authorities and the US-based National Hurricane Center warned.
It is not expected to make landfall but will remain very close to the coast, about 60 to 65 km away, and any change in its path closer to shore will increase the severity of its impact, the head of Mexico's weather agency Fabian Vazquez said at a press conference.
"Everyone in this region needs to be very careful and stay alert over the weekend," he added.
Mexico's civil protection agency asked residents to start preparations for the storm's arrival by securing doors and windows, and removing objects that could be thrown around by the strong winds.
"Trudy has the potential to even reach Category 4 or 5 intensity," said Alex DaSilva, a hurricane meteorologist at private forecaster AccuWeather.
Located about 235 miles (380 km) southwest of resort city Acapulco, the storm is expected to produce up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, according to the NHC.
HARD-HIT PACIFIC COAST The hurricane will strike Mexico's Pacific coast, a region that has already been battered in recent weeks by storms that left several dead and caused severe flooding.
"The most critical conditions will start on Saturday, with very severe winds and waves along the coast, in an area that has already been affected for several weeks," Vazquez said.
Tropical Storm Simon continues to weaken farther northwest offshore, after [USN:L1N45Y0H6 TEXT:"dropping heavy rain"] along the coast earlier as a hurricane.
Last week, tropical storm Rachel hit the Baja California peninsula damaging 1,500 homes, according to Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

items.title: Barril sube más de 3% para registrar alza semanal, mercado atento a suministro O.Medio
items.author: Arathy Somasekhar
items.creator: Arathy Somasekhar
items.summary: Los precios del petróleo subieron más de un 3% para registrar un avance semanal, debido a la continua incertidumbre sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio, mientras los inversionistas seguían evaluando la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia podría suministrar a los mercados mundiales.
items.body:
Los precios del petróleo subieron más de un 3% para registrar un avance semanal, debido a la continua incertidumbre sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio, mientras los inversionistas seguían evaluando la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia podría suministrar a los mercados mundiales.
* Los futuros del crudo Brent se disparaban 3 dólares a un máximo de sesión de 109,58 dólares el barril a las 1650 GMT, mientras que los futuros del crudo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) de Estados Unidos sumaban 3 dólares a un pico de jornada de 101,02 dólares y un máximo desde el 21 de septiembre.
En lo que va de semana, el Brent ha subido alrededor de un 4% y el WTI un 8,5%.
"El conflicto en Oriente Medio sigue reapareciendo y creo que es cuestionable la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia puede suministrar realmente a los mercados. Esos dos factores siguen impulsando a los operadores a comprar", afirmó Dennis Kissler, vicepresidente sénior de operaciones de BOK Financial.
* La inquietud por el suministro también aumentó al recrudecer los ataques en torno al estrecho de Ormuz durante los últimos 10 días, y con Irán afirmando que está intensificando los ataques en respuesta al bloqueo estadounidense de sus puertos y a las sanciones más duras introducidas el mes pasado.
* Los hutíes lanzaron el jueves misiles contra el complejo del palacio presidencial de Yemen, en la ciudad sureña de Adén, matando a dos guardias, mientras que la coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita en Yemen detalló decenas de ataques contra infraestructuras saudíes en el marco de este conflicto cada vez más intenso.
"La intensificación de los ataques iraníes provocó una fuerte caída de los flujos de crudo del Golfo", dijeron analistas de Kpler en un reporte el jueves, añadiendo que esperan una recuperación más lenta y desigual de los flujos por el estrecho de Ormuz a falta de un acuerdo político global.
Mientras tanto, Ucrania atacó el jueves una refinería de petróleo rusa después de que el presidente Volodimir Zelenski declarara que Kiev abandonaba el alto el fuego sobre las instalaciones energéticas anunciado por el presidente Donald Trump y criticara la disposición de este último a llegar a acuerdos con Moscú.
La refinería de petróleo rusa de Riazán ha suspendido las operaciones en una unidad de destilación primaria de crudo tras un ataque con drones en la región el jueves, informaron dos fuentes del sector a Reuters.
La AIE acordó el jueves liberar más de 20 millones de barriles de combustible al mercado.

items.title: Stellantis workers set to vote on potential strike action this weekend
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: Stellantis workers in Canada are set to vote this weekend on whether to authorize a strike as their union says contract negotiations with the automaker remain at a standstill.
items.body: TORONTO — Stellantis workers in Canada are set to vote this weekend on whether to authorize a strike as their union says contract negotiations with the automaker remain at a standstill. Unifor is holding the votes on Saturday and Sunday and plans to announce results at the start of next week. However, the union representing more than 9,000 Stellantis workers in Canada said it is hoping to avoid a potential strike. It said authorization for job action would provide leverage to help reach a negotiated agreement. “A strike authorization gives the bargaining committee the authority to call a strike if necessary, it does not automatically mean a strike will take place,” said a statement last week signed by Unifor national president Lana Payne and other members of the union’s bargaining committee. “Strike action remains a last resort, but the ability to strike is an important part of collective bargaining and can help create the conditions for an agreement.” The previous collective agreement between Stellantis and the union expired Sept. 20 without the two sides coming to terms on a new tentative deal. Unifor’s bargaining committee and the company are at an impasse over several key issues, including job security and the future of the Brampton, Ont., assembly plant Stellantis wants to sell. The fate of the Brampton plant, which has been idled since 2023, has been a central issue. Talks came to a standstill on Sept. 11 when Stellantis signed a memorandum of understanding with defence contractor Roshel for a potential sale of the facility. Stellantis Canada president and CEO Trevor Longley said in a September letter to employees that “market and trade conditions have directly impacted the original business case” for the plant, but that the move to sell could support future operations at the site. “Stellantis remains committed to bargaining in good faith and is prepared to continue discussions toward a negotiated agreement that recognizes the contributions of our employees while supporting the long-term competitiveness of our Canadian operations,” the automaker’s spokesperson LouAnn Gosselin in a statement this week. More than 2,000 workers were laid off from the Brampton plant when it halted operations in 2023. The facility had been slated to be retooled for Jeep production, a process that began early in 2024, before the company paused the plan in early 2025. It later announced it was moving production of the Jeep Compass to Illinois., leaving the plant idled indefinitely. Unifor has filed a grievance over that move, alleging it violated the previous collective agreement. For its part, Roshel has said it is willing to consider hiring laid-off workers from the plant as soon as this year “through the federal government’s Light Utility Vehicles procurement program and other automotive and defence opportunities.” Roshel CEO Roman Shimonov said the company plans to establish a Canadian Centre of Excellence for Defence Manufacturing in Brampton in addition to automotive production, which would involve more than 2,000 jobs. Payne has written to federal Industry Minister Mélanie Joly urging the government to block the potential sale and clarify whether the MOU breached Stellantis’ previous commitments to Ottawa. Last fall, Prime Minister Mark Carney said he had expressed disappointment during a conversation with the global head of Stellantis over the company moving Jeep Compass production to the United States. At the time, the prime minister said he reminded Stellantis of its commitments to the government under funding deals — such as keeping the Brampton plant — and warned there would be consequences if it failed to meet those obligations. Joly’s office did not respond to a request for comment. Contract talks began Sept. 1 in Toronto after Unifor ratified new collective agreements with Ford Motor Co. and General Motors in Canada earlier in the summer, as part of its pattern bargaining process with each of the Detroit Three. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 16, 2026. Sammy Hudes, The Canadian Press

Oct 16 : CoreWeave's shares and bond were set for steep weekly losses on Friday, underscoring investor worries over the cloud-computing company's $50 billion debt load that has rippled across the AI industry.
The Nvidia-backed company came into focus this week after the latest inflation data boosted bets on interest-rate hikes, raising the chances of higher payout on borrowings by data center and AI infrastructure firms with huge debt.
CoreWeave shares fell more than 11 per cent on Friday, taking their weekly losses to nearly 25 per cent. If the current levels hold, they are set for their worst week in over 11 months.
"Its not just CoreWeave, there's several (companies) that are falling into this category because of concerns that the revenue is just not going to be there to turn a profit and maintain the amount of debt that these companies are taking on," said Todd Schoenberger, chief investment officer at CrossCheck Management.

Investor worries over CoreWeave's massive debt load had a contagion affect that impacted rival Nebius Group, whose shares were set for their steepest weekly fall in two months.
Nebius dropped 10 per cent and data center operators Applied Digital and IREN slipped 9 per cent each.
The selloff is a stark reminder that AI companies' reliance on debt is becoming a risk for investors and punctures the notion that companies at the heart of the AI boom are immune to macroeconomic headwinds.
CoreWeave's stock has already lost about a fifth of its value, or nearly 9.6 billion, so far this month.
The steepest decline this week came on Wednesday, when the stock dropped 15.5 per cent. Short sellers made around $806 million, the fourth best single day for CoreWeave shorts since the stock listed in March 2025, according to data analytics firm ORTEX.
DEBT MARKET JITTERS
The yield on CoreWeave's October 2031 maturity dollar bond briefly surged past 16 per cent on Thursday. It is set to decline for a fifth straight week, down about 3 cents on the dollar this week.
The cost of insuring against CoreWeave's debt has surged past 1,000 basis points to record highs this week, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Still, several analysts were not ready to throw in the towel. Evercore analysts maintained their outperform rating on CoreWeave stock.
"The markets appear to be extrapolating a higher secondary-market bond yield as evidence the business model has stopped working, which we don't think is the case," they wrote in a note.
Given the circular nature of AI financing and Nvidia's stake in CoreWeave, Brian Reynolds, chief market strategist at Reynolds Strategy, said Nvidia could also offer buy it.
"At a small premium to the current stock price, but far below where the stock had been trading in the past," he said. "We understand that this may not be a likely option, but... it may not be far-fetched."
Nvidia is CoreWeave's second-largest investor and its CEO Jensen Huang recently gave the cloud company a vote of confidence, saying its financial strength was "improving every day".
But his endorsement is yet to lift CoreWeave's stock, a contrast from June when his support for Marvell Technology sent shares soaring.
Other analysts argued the rout in CoreWeave should not be seen as a sign that the AI rally is coming to an end.
"You cannot take CoreWeave as the poster child for AI," said Tommaso Leodari, chief investment officer at Dubai-based hedge fund Index & Cie.
Exchange traded funds managed by Cathie Wood's ARK Invest have been lapping up CoreWeave shares over the last two sessions, with total purchases exceeding 381,000 shares.
Retail investors have also bought into the weakness, buying up net $66 million worth of the stock so far this week, which is the second highest weekly figure on record, according to Vanda data.

items.author: Shashwat Chauhan, Niket Nishant
items.creator: Shashwat Chauhan, Niket Nishant
items.summary: CoreWeave's shares and bond were set for steep weekly losses on Friday, underscoring investor worries over the cloud-computing company's $50 billion debt load that has rippled across the AI industry.
items.body:
CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) shares and bond were set for steep weekly losses on Friday, underscoring investor worries over the cloud-computing company's $50 billion debt load that has rippled across the AI industry.
The Nvidia-backed company came into focus this week after the latest inflation data boosted bets on [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"interest-rate hikes"], raising the chances of higher payout on borrowings by data center and AI infrastructure firms with huge debt.
CoreWeave shares fell more than 11% on Friday, taking their weekly losses to nearly 25%. If the current levels hold, they are set for their worst week in over 11 months.
"Its not just CoreWeave, there's several (companies) that are falling into this category because of concerns that the revenue is just not going to be there to turn a profit and maintain the amount of debt that these companies are taking on," said Todd Schoenberger, chief investment officer at CrossCheck Management.
Investor worries over CoreWeave's massive debt load had a contagion affect that impacted rival Nebius Group (NBIS.O) , whose shares were set for their steepest weekly fall in two months.
Nebius (NBIS.O) dropped 10% and data center operators Applied Digital (APLD.O) and IREN (IREN.O) slipped 9% each.
The selloff is a stark reminder that AI companies' reliance on debt is becoming a risk for investors and punctures the notion that companies at the heart of the AI boom are immune to macroeconomic headwinds.
CoreWeave's stock has already lost about a fifth of its value, or nearly 9.6 billion, so far this month.
The steepest decline this week came on Wednesday, when the stock dropped 15.5%. Short sellers made around $806 million, the fourth best single day for CoreWeave shorts since the stock listed in March 2025, according to data analytics firm ORTEX.
DEBT MARKET JITTERS The yield on CoreWeave's October 2031 maturity dollar bond briefly surged past 16% on Thursday. It is set to decline for a fifth straight week, down about 3 cents on the dollar this week.
The cost of insuring against CoreWeave's debt has surged past 1,000 basis points to record highs this week, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Still, several analysts were not ready to throw in the towel. Evercore analysts maintained their outperform rating on CoreWeave stock.
"The markets appear to be extrapolating a higher secondary-market bond yield as evidence the business model has stopped working, which we don't think is the case," they wrote in a note.
Given the circular nature of AI financing and Nvidia's stake in CoreWeave, Brian Reynolds, chief market strategist at Reynolds Strategy, said Nvidia could also offer buy it.
"At a small premium to the current stock price, but far below where the stock had been trading in the past," he said. "We understand that this may not be a likely option, but... it may not be far-fetched."
Nvidia is CoreWeave's second-largest investor and its CEO Jensen Huang recently gave the cloud company [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"a vote of confidence"], saying its financial strength was "improving every day".
But his endorsement is yet to lift CoreWeave's stock, a contrast from June when his support for Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) [USN:L4N42A0MP TEXT:"sent shares soaring"].
Other analysts argued the rout in CoreWeave should not be seen as a sign that the AI rally is coming to an end.
"You cannot take CoreWeave as the poster child for AI," said Tommaso Leodari, chief investment officer at Dubai-based hedge fund Index & Cie.
Exchange traded funds managed by Cathie Wood's ARK Invest have been lapping up CoreWeave shares over the last two sessions, with total purchases exceeding 381,000 shares.
Retail investors have also bought into the weakness, buying up net $66 million worth of the stock so far this week, which is the second highest weekly figure on record, according to Vanda data.

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 16 : Blue Origin is targeting multiple flights per week of its New Glenn rocket by the end of the decade, a company executive said on Friday, as it spends billions of dollars on infrastructure needed to match rival SpaceX's launch dominance.
Jeff Bezos' space firm also plans to add more launch and landing pads in Florida for New Glenn, its flagship heavy-lift orbital rocket that has been grounded for the year since exploding on the company's only launchpad in May.
Blue Origin has invested over $3 billion to date in its sprawling Florida production and rocket integration facilities that span roughly 31 acres with some 5,000 employees, Ian Richardson, senior vice president of operations, said in a company blog post.
A $330 million expansion to those facilities will support production of a heavier-lift version of the rocket, New Glenn 9x4, and is targeted for completion in the summer of 2027, Richardson said, adding it will allow annual production of up to 150 upper stages of the rocket.

"These investments are centered on one goal: building the capacity to support more missions, more reliably, and more efficiently," Richardson said. "As we look ahead, this infrastructure is designed to support multiple flights per week by the end of the decade."
The New Glenn explosion in May, which happened days before a planned launch of Amazon satellites, badly damaged the company's Florida launchpad, where the 30-storey-tall (322 feet) rocket had lifted off three times since its 2025 debut.
New Glenn is expected to return to flight early next year.
Its last flight, in April, was its first mission failure when an issue with the rocket's second stage put a satellite from its customer AST SpaceMobile into the wrong orbit, causing it to fall back into Earth's atmosphere.
Blue Origin is one of the main launch providers for Amazon's budding satellite internet constellation, Leo, which will rival SpaceX's Starlink.
New Glenn's explosion upended Amazon's launch schedule with the rocket, tightening a global launch squeeze that has left dozens of satellite companies desperate for rides to space.
Blue Origin has been pressed to return the rocket to its pad, with CEO Dave Limp seeing it as the company's top priority among an array of other programs, including a multibillion-dollar NASA assignment to build a lunar lander that will return astronauts to the moon.
Elon Musk's SpaceX, the world's most active launch provider, had 165 Falcon missions last year, mostly carrying its in-house Starlink satellites. Musk envisions launching hundreds of missions per year with Starship, the company's next-generation rocket.

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 16 : Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms.
AI-linked stocks, central to the bull market that just marked its four-year anniversary, struggled in recent days, with sharp declines in shares of semiconductor companies and tech hardware firms such as Dell Technologies.
Meta, among the hyperscalers spending massively to build AI data centers, highlights the upcoming week of quarterly reports, along with semiconductor firms Lam Research and Texas Instruments.
"It certainly feels like the narrative in the market is a little bit jittery," said Garrett Melson, portfolio strategist with Natixis Investment Managers Solutions. "Clearly there's a lot of uncertainty around where AI stands right now."

Worries rippled through markets over risks tied to the financing of the AI build-out boom, which has lifted profits for a wide swath of companies and boosted economic growth. Investors were watching developments with CoreWeave, an AI cloud company with about $50 billion in debt. This week, its shares tumbled.
In other recent signs of caution, strategists at Deutsche Bank and RBC Capital Markets separately pulled back on their recommendations of the tech sector. On October 9, Deutsche Bank strategists said the rotation into tech had "run far and the risk-reward no longer looks favorable in the near term."
Despite the swoon in heavyweight tech and AI stocks, the S&P 500 remained down only about 1 per cent from its record high set this month. Other sectors, which lagged as tech soared in recent weeks, were now picking up the slack.  
"This is very much an on-off switch type of market," Melson said. "When AI is working, it sucks all the oxygen out of the room for the rest of the sectors."
META KICKS OFF HYPERSCALER RESULTS
US reporting season heats up next week, with investors counting on robust performance. S&P 500 companies are expected to have increased earnings by more than 30 per cent in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES.
Massive outlays on AI data centers and infrastructure underpin the profit jump. Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers that combined are expected to increase their capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs. Investors are eager for signs the companies can show returns on the investments, which would build confidence that the spending is sustainable.
"One of the most important takeaways of earnings season is whether or not the profitability of the hyperscalers can grow faster than the pace of their capex," said Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth.
Meta, whose market capitalization was about $1.9 trillion, has seen its shares climb in recent weeks as it launched its Muse AI assistant.
"With the cost of capital going up, this capex blowout is going to become more expensive, which raises the bar for returns," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services. "Meta is going to be the first up to try to provide some color around that question."
SEMIS, TESLA, NETFLIX ALSO ON TAP
Chip companies have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the capital spending boom, but the stocks have cooled off. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index has slumped 8 per cent this month, although it remained up more than 60 per cent on the year, compared to a 13 per cent year-to-date gain for the S&P 500. 
Investors will look to Wednesday's reports from Lam Research and Texas Instruments for broader indications of demand in the semiconductor industry. Both companies' share prices are up some 60 per cent in 2026.
Elsewhere, investors will focus on results from Elon Musk's Tesla, another signature stock of the tech bull market. Streaming giant Netflix, consumer products company Procter & Gamble and engine maker GE Aerospace are among other high-profile reports in the coming week.
The rise in Treasury yields and prospects for further rate hikes from the Federal Reserve also remain front-burner issues for stock investors. Hot inflation data this week boosted bets on another rate increase at the Fed's meeting at the end of October. Futures pricing suggested most investors still expect the US central bank to wait until its meeting in December to raise rates for a second time this year.
"Another strong earnings season should help equities withstand moderately higher rates," analysts at UBS Global Wealth Management said in a note on Thursday.

items.title: CoreWeave bond rout tests market's math on AI buildout
items.author: Suzanne McGee, Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
items.creator: Suzanne McGee, Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
items.summary: A sharp decline in CoreWeave's bonds this week is emerging as a test of investors' willingness to keep financing the massive buildout of AI infrastructure, as rising borrowing costs and scrutiny of debt-funded expansion hit the sector.
items.body:
A sharp decline in CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) bonds this week is emerging as a test of investors' willingness to keep financing the massive buildout of AI infrastructure, as rising borrowing costs and scrutiny of debt-funded expansion hit the sector.
Analysts and portfolio managers said the selloff in the data center operator's debt carries more significance than a concurrent rout in its shares because it may signal a broader reassessment of the risks tied to financing AI projects that may take years to generate revenue.
CoreWeave bonds issued in June at a yield of 9.675% have plunged in value, sending their yield to 15% this week.
"CoreWeave is absolutely the canary in the coal mine" for a market segment that is coming under more stress, said Max Frumes, global head of distressed and leveraged finance at 9fin, a fintech corporate credit data and analytics company.
"This is going to be a turning point in the pricing and availability and structure of credit that's supporting the AI boom," said Frumes, who believes that other AI-linked debt will follow CoreWeave into distressed territory. "It's going to get more expensive. There will be a lot more scrutiny and probably some pushback from investors."
CoreWeave shares fell 15.1% from Monday's open through Thursday's close, despite a 6% gain on Thursday after a [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"vote of confidence from partner Nvidia NVDA.O"]. The decline was broadly in line with weakness in other so-called neocloud companies such as Nebius (NBIS.O) and Iren (IREN.O) .
Credit investors said they already are [USN:L6N45611M TEXT:"becoming more selective"].
"We're definitely taking another look at our exposures across the AI infrastructure space, particularly where the risks are concentrated and whether we're being adequately compensated for taking them," said John Han, a portfolio manager at fixed-income asset management firm F/m Investments.
F/m's portfolio contains unsecured CoreWeave bonds in one of its exchange-traded funds, but only because they make up part of the index tracked by the ETF. At their current yields those bonds "certainly deserve another look," Han said. He generally prefers to invest in high-yield securities via special purpose vehicles that may offer lower yields but also more collateral and less risk.
"The market is being very selective and really singling out anything that has more leverage, and (that may be) in a bit more challenging operating environment," said Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager of fixed income at Catalyst funds.
To Holzenthaler and other investors, what the markets are witnessing now is an overreaction as sentiment shifts from being overly upbeat to downright bearish.
In June, the risks driving the selloff -- the sheer size of the funding needs, the leverage, the reliance on outside financing, the risk that the GPUs (graphics processing units) being purchased for data centers would be obsolete before the new facilities could open -- were merely overlooked or downplayed.
"A few months ago, I would have said people were just too optimistic around AI," Holzenthaler said.
Deutsche Bank global head of macro and thematic research Jim Reid sees the market entering a new phase in which debt financing is becoming increasingly important.
"As we move to a capex cycle funded out of debt rather than simply free cash flow, we have to increasingly respect the credit price action," Reid wrote in a recent report. "AI financing costs aren't dramatic overall, but there are worrying themes at the edges."
Vanguard bond portfolio manager Brad Collins said assessing AI-related debt has become more challenging as issuers bring increasingly large and varied offerings to market, often forcing investors to make decisions in days or even hours.
Rising inflation has pushed financing costs higher overall and fueled concern about what lies ahead for mammoth AI capital spending plans. Then there is the [USN:L6N43G12P TEXT:"growing political controversy"] surrounding the construction of data centers.
Even one of the tech sector's stalwarts allows that the road ahead may be bumpy at times. Dan Ives, partner and technology analyst at Yorkville Ives, an investment firm, estimates that 5% to 10% of planned projects ultimately will not be built.
"The growing noise around data center permitting and midterm rhetoric on power prices has given investors another reason to step back," Ives said.

items.body:
［ロンドン　１６日　ロイター］ - ＢｏｆＡグローバル・リサーチによると、投資家は１４日までの１週間に現金を減らし、債券と株式に資金を投じた。

ＢｏｆＡがＥＰＦＲのデータを基にまとめた世界市場の週間資金フローは以下の通り。

・株式ファンドには６４５億ドル流入。

・ハイテク株に１０７億ドル流入した。年初来の流入額は過去最高の１９６０億ドル。米国株には３９１億ドル流入し、年初来では過去最高の６３６０億ドル。

・ハイテク株はここ数営業日、荒い値動きが続いており、ナスダック総合指数は１５日に１．８％下落した。同日、国債価格は急伸し、米１０年債利回りは１０ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下した。ただ、国債はここ数カ月、売られ続けていた。

・債券には１１８億ドル流入。米国債には３６億ドルが流入し、１６週連続の流入。連続流入期間は２０２４年８月以来の長さ。米債券運用大手ＰＩＭＣＯのシニアアドバイザーは先週、売り込まれた米国債は「極めて割安」だと述べていた。

・「キャッシュ」と呼ばれるＭＭＦからは５３１億ドルが流出。

・新興国市場には１７７億ドルが流入。このうち中国が８６億ドルだった。

・ブラジルにはこの２週間で過去最高の４７億ドルが流入。１０月上旬に行われたブラジル大統領選の第１回投票では、右派のボルソナロ上院議員が予想を上回る得票。同氏は左派のルラ大統領と決選投票で争う。

items.title: 経産省、台湾ＴＳＭＣの3ナノ半導体生産計画を認定　熊本第2工場
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 １６日 ロイター] - 経済産業省は１６日、半導体受託生産の世界最大手、台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が熊本県に建設中の第２工場で回路線幅３ナノメートル（ナノは１０億分の１）の先端半導体を生産するための計画変更を認定した。従来は６ナノや１２ナノ、４０ナノを計画していたが、変更後は３ナノに専念する。

現時点での生産枚数は月６０００枚を計画しているが、今後、日本政府の支援を前提に具体的数量を検討する。経産省は来年度予算で支援資金を要求中で、既に生産開始している第１工場を含む最大助成額は１兆円を超える見通し。

経産省の南部友成・情報産業課長は記者団に「これからのＡＩ（人工知能）トランスフォーメーションを考えれば、ＡＩ自体を支える３ナノの最先端ロジック半導体は必要不可欠だ」と指摘。国内に３ナノの生産拠点を確保することは「日本のサプライチェーン強靭化や経済安全保障の強化にとって非常に有意義だ」と述べた。

ＴＳＭＣの魏哲家最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２月、高市早苗首相と会談した際、第２工場で３ナノ半導体を生産する計画を伝えていた。同社は、今回の計画変更で熊本県の第１、第２工場への設備投資額が計２３０億ドル（約３兆６３００億円）を超える見込みとし「日本と世界中の顧客に先端技術を提供し、ＡＩ時代における強力な需要に対応していく」とコメントした。

items.title: 中国人民銀総裁、金融市場開放加速と人民元国際化推進表明
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［北京／上海　１６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［北京／上海　１６日　ロイター］ - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）の潘功勝総裁は、巨大な国内金融市場の一段の対外開放を進める方針を示し、人民元建て資産は世界の投資家の間で高まる分散投資ニーズに応えることができると表明した。国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行総裁が開かれているタイのバンコクで１５日に行った講演内容を、人民銀行が発表した。

潘氏は講演で、地政学リスクの高まりや世界経済の構造的な変化、人工知能（ＡＩ）の急速な進展に言及した。

「中国の着実な経済成長とハイテク産業の急速な発展は、人民元資産の確固たる支えとなる」と述べ、人民銀が投融資を促進するため、引き続きリスク管理ツールの拡充を進める方針を示した。

トランプ米大統領の関税措置や予測困難な外交政策によってドル資産の信認が損なわれる中、中国は資本市場の対外開放と人民元の国際化を推進する取り組みを強化している。

潘氏は、人民元建て債券が適格担保として世界的に受容され活用が拡大することを推進し、国境を越えた金融インフラの接続性を強化し、オフショア人民元市場の発展を支援すると表明した。

Britain's financial watchdog said on Friday it had revoked bans on four former traders previously sanctioned over the LIBOR and EURIBOR manipulation scandal after the Court of Appeal overturned their convictions earlier this month.

items.body:
Miho Uranaka

[東京 １６日 ロイター] - 香港のアクティビスト（物言う株主）ファンド、オアシス・マネジメントのセス・フィッシャー最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）は１６日、都内で開催したチャリティイベントで、９％の株式保有を公表しているニデックについて、足元では保有比率がさらに高まっていることを明らかにした。その上で、条件次第では、保有比率を大幅に引き上げる可能性があるとの考えを示した。

フィッシャー氏は、「（昨日提出した）大量保有報告書では、同社株の保有比率は９％だが、現在はそれをやや上回っている。 大量保有報告書でも説明しているとおり、株価やその他の要因次第では保有比率を大幅に引き上げる可能性がある」と述べた。オアシスは１５日提出の報告書で、ニデック株について、５％超取得行為を予定していると明記していた。

数週間前に開かれたニデックの記者会見について「何をすべきかや、どのような措置を講じたのかについて十分な説明がなかった」と指摘。問題に直接関与した人物の処分や組織改革が遅れていることについて、「非常にがっかりしている」と語った。

同氏は、ニデックには取締役会レベルでの監督機能強化が必要との認識を示し、オアシスが取締役候補を提案しているという。会社側が迅速に対応しなければ、臨時株主総会（ＥＧＭ）の開催を求める可能性があると警告した。

さらに、ニデックは内部統制やコンプライアンス体制の整備を進める一方で、非公開化を含む戦略的な選択肢についても並行して検討すべきだと主張。「望まない形での上場廃止に追い込まれるリスクがある。それは株主や従業員にとって受け入れられない」と話した。

items.title: ＡＩ、安全策なければリスクが恩恵上回る恐れ＝ＩＭＦ専務理事
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrea Shalal　Maria Martinez

[バンコク １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Andrea Shalal　Maria Martinez

[バンコク １６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のゲオルギエワ専務理事は１６日、人工知能（ＡＩ）に適切な安全策や倫理的な枠組みを設けなければ、リスクが恩恵を上回る恐れがあると述べた。業界の自主規制に主要国政府の関与を組み合わせる考えを支持した。

米ＡＩ開発企業アンソロピック共同創業者のジャック・クラーク氏も参加したパネル討論で発言した。ＡＩは既に世界経済を押し上げているが、生産性の大幅な向上が期待されたほど早く実現しなければ、経済にマイナスのショックを及ぼす恐れもあると述べた。

「安全策がなければ、リスクが恩恵を上回るかもしれない。何よりも倫理的な基盤が必要だが、社会としてそこまで達しているかどうか、確信が持てない」と語った。

急速に進化するＡＩの恩恵を世界中の人々が受けるには、デジタルインフラや電力を利用できる環境、適切な規制といった一定の条件を整える必要があるとした。

また、これほど速く進化する技術にどう安全策を設けるかが、今やより大きな課題だと指摘。ＡＩの開発状況を、観客を守る防護柵がない中を猛スピードで走るＦ１マシンに例えた。

＜常識に即した基準＞

ゲオルギエワ氏は、絶えず変化するこの分野を規制・監督するのに政府は向いていないため、業界の自主規制が適切だと述べた。ただ社会との対話も必要だとした。米国、中国、インドなどＡＩ産業の規模が大きい国々に加え、ＡＩのサプライチェーン（供給網）に関わる国々も関与すべきだと語った。

ＩＭＦのような機関も、生産性の伸び、労働市場、金融安定へのリスクなど、それぞれの専門分野で関与すべきだと述べた。

クラーク氏は基準づくりは可能であり、欧州連合（ＥＵ）の初期段階の政策枠組みや米国での自主的な取り組みを通じ、既に始まりつつあると主張した。

同氏はアンソロピックが自社システムを定期的に試験し、試験の詳細を公表して情報を共有していると説明した。ただ、こうした取り組みを完全に自主性に委ねるべきではないとの考えを示した。

ＡＩを開発する国々による規制に賛成するかと問われると、「賛成だ。常識に即した基準が必要だ。それが最終的に技術への信頼を生み、経済を発展させる」と答えた。

また、アンソロピックは第三者の評価者を受け入れ、データを調べる権限を与えていると説明した。「最終的には、他の多くの企業もそうする必要があると考えている」と述べ、イーロン・マスク氏が自身の会社スペースＸも同様の取り組みを行う可能性に言及したことを歓迎した。

ブラウン米財務次官（国際担当）は別の記者会見で、ＩＭＦは世界経済のリスクに目を向け過ぎており、ＡＩのように経済にプラスのショックをもたらす可能性をもっと重視すべきだと述べた。

イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）のベイリー総裁は国際金融協会（ＩＩＦ）の会合で、ＡＩの試験基準を巡って各国の足並みがそろうことについて、１カ月前より楽観的になったと述べた。

別のパネル討論で、ドイツ連邦銀行（中銀）のナーゲル総裁が、ＡＩは世界の不均衡を拡大させる可能性があると述べた。「ハードウエアとソフトウエア開発の両面でＡＩに巨額の投資が必要なことを考えれば、それは明らかだ」と語った。

ハーバード大学の経済学者ダニ・ロドリック氏は、ＡＩによる生産性向上が実現するかどうかは分からず、もろ刃の剣になっていると指摘した。先週、ベルリンで開かれた学際的な会議の後、ロイターに語った。

生産性が向上すれば、影響を受ける業種で大規模な雇用喪失が起き、職を追われる人が出る可能性がある。一方、向上しなければ、データセンターへの巨額投資が多大な損失を伴う金融面の調整を引き起こしかねないと述べた。「雇用危機か金融危機か、どちらに対処することになるのか分からない」と語った。

items.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝反発、ＡＩ企業の自社株買い好感　当局の支援観測
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１６日 ロイター] - 中国株式市場は反発。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連企業が相次いで自社株買いや好調な業績見通しを発表したことが支えとなった。ただ、週間では３カ月ぶりの大幅な下げとなった。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は０．１％高で終了。上海総合指数は０．２％高。ただ、ＣＳＩ３００指数は週間では３．４％下落し、７月中旬以来の大幅な下げ。１０週連続の下落となった。

ハイテク株は下げ止まった。光トランシーバーメーカーの蘇州旭創科技（イオプトリンク）や半導体製造装置メーカーの北京屹唐半導体科技（パイオテック）など、少なくとも１０社のＡＩサプライチェーン関連企業が自社株買いや株式取得計画を発表した。

また半導体メーカーの沐曦集成電路（メタエックス）などハイテク企業が相次いで、高成長を示す第３・四半期の業績予想を発表した。

items.title: 中国、ＡＩなど40技術で輸出規制案　対象外設定で企業に海外展開余地
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Eduardo Baptista

［北京　１６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Eduardo Baptista

［北京　１６日　ロイター］ - 中国商務省は１６日、人工知能（ＡＩ）モデル、ＡＩエージェント、計算クラスターに関わる技術など、ＡＩ分野の２３技術を対象とする輸出規制案を発表した。最先端技術の開発を巡り米国との競争が激しくなるなか、不可欠と見なす技術の移転を制限する最新の動きとなる。

改定案は、ＡＩのほかバイオ医薬、太陽光発電の分野など４０の技術を対象としている。１１月１５日まで一般から意見を募る。同時に、対象となる技術には暫定措置として輸出前の登録制度を導入する。

商務省は今回の改定について、機微な分野で関連技術の応用が広がり続けていることを理由に挙げた。また特定の国や地域、組織を狙い撃ちした措置ではないと説明した。

改定案では、制限対象技術を含むＡＩモデルの海外展開を対象とする一方、アプリケーション・プログラミング・インターフェース（ＡＰＩ）、ウェブサイト、アプリ、サービスとしてのソフトウエア（ＳａａＳ）プラットフォーム経由でのアクセスは対象外とする。

この区分けにより、ディープシークやアリババといった中国のＡＩ開発企業による海外展開の余地が残される一方、中国政府は機微なＡＩ技術の海外移転に対する監督を強められる見通し。

ディープシークの「Ｒ１」モデルが２０２５年に登場して以降、中国製ＡＩモデルは低価格と性能改善を背景に海外で存在感を高めている。ＡＩ分野の管理をどこまで厳格化するかを決める上で、中国政府にとって重みを増している。

ロイターは７月、中国当局がアリババ、バイトダンスなど主要テクノロジー企業と、未公開のものを含む中国の最先端人工知能（ＡＩ）モデルへの海外からのアクセスを制限する可能性について協議したと報じていた。

商務省は１６日、悪意あるソフトウエアを自律的に生成・改変できるシステムなどＡＩ技術の悪用防止も規制の目的と説明。大半のＡＩ技術は引き続き自由に輸出できるとし、オープンソース技術の輸出や中国企業が自社で運営する海外のコンピューティングセンターは簡素化した許可手続きを適用する。オープンソースでの公開や学術論文ですでに知られている技術は規制案の対象外になる。

改定案には、一部の新規細胞・遺伝子治療と低分子干渉ＲＮＡ（ｓｉＲＮＡ）技術に関する知的財産権の移転を禁じる内容も盛り込まれている。

items.title: China's central bank to further open its financial markets to foreigners, chief says
items.author: Samuel Shen, Selena Li
items.creator: Samuel Shen, Selena Li
items.summary: China's central bank chief pledged to further open up the country's vast financial markets, saying in a speech that yuan assets can meet global investors' growing need for diversification amid trade uncertainty.
items.body:
China's central bank chief pledged to further open up the country's vast financial markets, saying in a speech that yuan assets can meet global investors' growing need for diversification amid trade uncertainty.
Bank Governor Pan Gongsheng cited rising geopolitical risks, profound changes in the global economic landscape and rapid advances in AI as reasons for China to continue promoting yuan internationalization.
"China’s steady economic growth, and rapid development of high-tech industries provide solid support for RMB assets," a People’s Bank of China (PBOC) statement quoted Pan as saying in a Thursday speech given on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
The remarks came a day after IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said China [USN:S0N40K04E TEXT:"must pivot"] from export-led growth towards more domestic consumption.
In Pan's speech, given to international policymakers at the annual meeting, he also called for Beijing to "shift from exports more toward domestic consumption," according to the statement.
TURBULENT MARKETS China has stepped up efforts to open its capital markets, at a time when US President Donald Trump's trade war and unpredictable foreign policies have dented trust in dollar assets.
Global financial markets have also become more turbulent as investors increasingly worry about whether companies embarking on massive investment in AI will manage to make sufficient earnings gains amid higher borrowing costs.
Pan said the PBOC will promote broader global acceptance and use of yuan bonds as eligible collateral, strengthen cross-border financial infrastructure connectivity and support the development of offshore yuan markets.
The bank will continue to expand risk management tools to expedite investment and financing, according to the statement.
In a separate speech on Friday, the central bank chief said global economic imbalances "are closely linked to the evolution of the global division of labor, inherent contradictions in the international monetary system, and factors such as chronic high fiscal deficits and high consumption in some countries," according to a separate PBOC statement.
"Global imbalances cannot be corrected through exchange rate adjustments," Pan said at the Friday meeting with European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde and Valdis Dombrovskis, the European Commissioner for Economy and Productivity, the statement said.

items.title: 情報ＢＯＸ：インドネシア「スタンドアローン」に格下げも、ＭＳＣＩの市場分類とは
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ジャカルタ　１６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ジャカルタ　１６日　ロイター］ - 指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩは１６日、インドネシア株式市場を「エマージング（新興国）市場」から「スタンドアローン」に格下げすることを検討していると発表した。以前警告していた「フロンティア市場」への格下げよりも厳しいもので、株や通貨ルピアは急落した。

ＭＳＣＩは、経済発展の水準、市場の規模と流動性、投資家に対する開放度に基づき、指数を４つのカテゴリーに分類している。概要は以下の通り。

＜先進国市場＞

最も成熟し、アクセスしやすい株式市場が対象。海外投資家の参加が事実上制限されておらず、資本の流れが非常に大きく、効率的な取引システムと安定した規制の枠組みを備える。この分類に入るには、１人当たり国民総所得（ＧＮＩ）が３年連続で世界銀行の高所得国基準を２５％上回る必要がある。

米国、日本、シンガポールがこの分類に含まれる。

＜新興国市場＞

経済発展に関する要件はないが、この区分に入るのは通常、新興国経済と見なされる国だ。「新興国市場」は、海外投資家に対する開放度が高く、資本移動も容易だが、「先進国市場」と比べるとなお一定の制約がある市場が対象となる。また、十分に機能し実績のある取引運営の枠組みを備えていることなども求められる。

ブラジル、中国、インド、韓国などが含まれる。インドネシアもその一つだが、同国の指数ウエートは２０２６年初めの１．１６％から９月末には０．４％に低下した。

＜フロンティア市場＞

比較的規模が小さく、発展が遅れている、あるいはアクセスしにくい市場が対象。ＭＳＣＩの組み入れ要件を満たす企業が１社あればよく、外国人投資家にある程度開放され、資本の出入りが少なくとも部分的に可能で、取引がそれなりに効率的であり、安定した制度的枠組みを備えていることが求められる。この分類には「アドバンスト・フロンティア市場」という下位区分がある。これは投資家にとってのアクセス性は高いものの、規模と流動性が限られる市場だ。

フロンティア市場にはベトナム、パキスタン、モロッコなどが含まれる。アドバンスト・フロンティア市場にはラトビアやエストニアといった欧州諸国が含まれる。

＜スタンドアローン市場＞

「スタンドアローン市場」指数は、対象市場を「新興国」や「フロンティア」の指数には組み入れないが、規模と流動性についてはそれらの基準を用いる。市場へのアクセス性や規模、流動性が著しく悪化した場合、「スタンドアローン市場」に再分類されることがある。新たに適格となった市場もこの分類に入る。

アルゼンチン、パナマ、ウクライナなどが「スタンドアローン」に分類されている。インドネシアがこの分類に移れば、経済規模で同グループ最大となり、２番目に大きいアルゼンチンの２倍以上となる。

＜新興国市場＞

経済発展に関する要件はないが、この区分に入るのは通常、新興国経済と見なされる国だ。「新興国市場」は、海外投資家に対する開放度が高く、資本移動も容易だが、「先進国市場」と比べるとなお一定の制約がある市場が対象となる。また、十分に機能し実績のある取引運営の枠組みを備えていることなども求められる。

ブラジル、中国、インド、韓国などが含まれる。インドネシアもその一つだが、同国の指数ウエートは２０２６年初めの１．１６％から９月末には０．４％に低下した。

＜フロンティア市場＞

比較的規模が小さく、発展が遅れている、あるいはアクセスしにくい市場が対象。ＭＳＣＩの組み入れ要件を満たす企業が１社あればよく、外国人投資家にある程度開放され、資本の出入りが少なくとも部分的に可能で、取引がそれなりに効率的であり、安定した制度的枠組みを備えていることが求められる。この分類には「アドバンスト・フロンティア市場」という下位区分がある。これは投資家にとってのアクセス性は高いものの、規模と流動性が限られる市場だ。

フロンティア市場にはベトナム、パキスタン、モロッコなどが含まれる。アドバンスト・フロンティア市場にはラトビアやエストニアといった欧州諸国が含まれる。

＜スタンドアローン市場＞

「スタンドアローン市場」指数は、対象市場を「新興国」や「フロンティア」の指数には組み入れないが、規模と流動性についてはそれらの基準を用いる。市場へのアクセス性や規模、流動性が著しく悪化した場合、「スタンドアローン市場」に再分類されることがある。新たに適格となった市場もこの分類に入る。

アルゼンチン、パナマ、ウクライナなどが「スタンドアローン」に分類されている。インドネシアがこの分類に移れば、経済規模で同グループ最大となり、２番目に大きいアルゼンチンの２倍以上となる。

items.title: マン・グループ、運用資産が過去最高の2709億ドル
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ロンドン １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ロンドン １６日 ロイター] - 大手ヘッジファンドのマン・グループが１６日発表した９月末の運用資産残高は、過去最高の２７０９億ドルとなった。６月末比では６．８％増えた。市場の変動が激しくなる中で資金流入が進んだ。発表後、株価は３％上昇した。

シティによると、運用資産残高は前年同期比２６％増加し、市場予想の２６３０億ドルを上回った。

第３・四半期の資金流入額は１０１億ドルと、予想を上回った。このうちオルタナティブファンドへの流入が１９億ドル、買い持ち戦略のファンド（ロング・オンリー・ファンド）への流入が８２億ドルだった。

運用資産残高の増加額のうち、５９億ドルは運用益によるものだった。

シティは今回の結果を好調と評価した。「市場の変動が激しさを増し、流動性の高いオルタナティブ投資に対する投資家の需要が拡大する中、マン・グループは特に恩恵を受ける企業の一つとみている」と述べた。

items.title: Tesla's new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, won't land until 2028
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Powered by rocket-style thrusters, Tesla's new Roadster raced upside down along a ramp, launched into a mid-air flip and landed back on its wheels.
items.body:
Advertisement

World

Tesla's new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, won't land until 2028

Powered by rocket-style thrusters, Tesla's new Roadster raced upside down along a ramp, launched into a mid-air flip and landed back on its wheels.

Tesla unveils its long-delayed Roadster nearly a decade after first revealing a next-generation version of its original electric sports car, at a launch event in Waco, Texas, US, on Oct 15, 2026, in this still image taken from a handout video. (Image: Tesla/Handout via Reuters)

FAST

SAN FRANCISCO: Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster powered with rocket-style thrusters on Thursday (Oct 15) and said it would start production in 2028, more than a decade after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car.
The white two-seater vehicle, developed in collaboration with CEO Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX, drove upside down on a ramp using a suction system, turned in the air and landed using built-in thrusters.
Later in the event it used the thrusters to jump over a truck and other vehicles, twisting in the air during the maneuver.
Some watchers saw the collaboration as Musk drumming up interest in a merger of the two big companies he controls, an idea he has explored by discussing their overlap.

The reveal gives Tesla a showpiece car after years of missed Roadster deadlines, but it comes as the company shifts its focus to self-driving technology and robotics, and days before third-quarter results that analysts say matter more to investors.
"It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, said on social media platform X.
"The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) and (SpaceX) together," Munster said.
Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the needle in a major way financially".
But the car still carries symbolic weight.

"Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month.
Viewers and witnesses gushed over the spectacle of the launch.
"That was the most insane product demo I've ever seen," Tesla fan and investor Sawyer Merritt posted on X. "I just saw this in person, and I'm still asking how this wasn't AI."
Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of US$200,000 for the vehicle.
Tesla's reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday's event showed a "Performance" version of the vehicle requiring a US$50,000 deposit and a "Thrust" version with "acceleration thrusters" requiring a US$250,000 deposit. A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla says is "invite only", is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system".
"HALFWAY TO THE SPEED OF SOUND" The event at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, had all the elements of a classic Musk product reveal: Dramatic music, smoke, mechanical hissing sounds and a launch countdown.
"This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX engineers working closely together to make something that you haven't seen in any movie," Musk, wearing a silver Western-style belt buckle emblazoned with the Tesla logo, told a cheering crowd of enthusiasts and investors.
The Roadster can accelerate from zero to 97 kmh in less than one second and can hit a top speed of over 370 kmh, Tesla vehicle engineering chief Lars Moravy said.

Tesla unveils its long-delayed Roadster nearly a decade after first revealing a next-generation version of its original electric sports car, at a launch event in Waco, Texas, US, on Oct 15, 2026, in this still image taken from a handout video. (Image: Tesla/Handout via Reuters)

Tesla unveils its long-delayed Roadster nearly a decade after first revealing a next-generation version of its original electric sports car, at a launch event in Waco, Texas, US, on Oct 15, 2026, in this still image taken from a handout video. (Image: Tesla/Handout via Reuters)

"Definitely much faster than that," an excited Musk said. "I think you've got to crack halfway to the speed of sound."
The Roadster can also travel over 480km on a single charge. That is less than half of what Musk promised in 2017, when Tesla first revealed a prototype of the second-generation Roadster and said that deliveries would begin in 2020.
The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever electric vehicle and used a Lotus Elise chassis. It helped change the world's view of what an EV could be. The company has since been known for its Model Y and Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans.
The reveal of the second-generation Roadster comes amid a sharp shift in Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, from manufacturing cars for human drivers.
This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. It also launched Cybercab - a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors.
Tesla is set to report third-quarter results on Oct 21.
Sales of Tesla's aging lineup of EVs have declined over the past two years, although high gas prices helped boost deliveries in the third quarter.
"The margin and cash flow numbers will carry far more weight with investors than anything they saw at the reveal," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for Asia-Pacific at trading platform eToro.

Source: Reuters/lk

items.title: ＡＩがインド組織のシステムに侵入、機密記録閲覧　印当局が公表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Munsif Vengattil

[ベンガルール １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Munsif Vengattil

[ベンガルール １６日 ロイター] - インドのサイバーセキュリティー当局は、試験中の人工知能（ＡＩ）モデルがインド組織の稼働中のシステムに侵入し、検知されないまま機密記録を閲覧していたと明らかにした。世界各地でＡＩが制御を逸脱する事例が相次ぐ中、インド当局がこうした事案を公式に発表したのは初めて。

インドのコンピューター緊急対応チーム（ＣＥＲＴ─Ｉｎ）は１５日遅く、ＡＩモデルの提供企業が、試験運用中に自社のＡＩエージェントが「割り当てられた業務の権限を逸脱」し、業務記録を含むインド企業のデータにアクセスしたと自主的に開示したことを明らかにした。ＡＩ提供企業や被害を受けた組織の名称は明かしていない。

ＣＥＲＴ─Ｉｎによると、被害を受けたインドの組織はいずれも侵入を自ら検知できず、全ての事案でＡＩ企業側が報告したという。

items.title: 中国財政相、ＥＵとの対話に意欲　マクロ経済政策の協調呼びかけ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [北京 １６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[北京 １６日 ロイター] - 中国の藍仏安財政相は１６日、バンコクで欧州連合（ＥＵ）高官と会談した。世界経済のガバナンスやマクロ経済政策の協調を巡り、意思疎通を深めるためＥＵと対話する用意があると表明した。

会談にはＥＵのドムブロフスキス欧州委員（経済・生産性担当）、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁、ユーロ圏財務相会合（ユーログループ）のピエラカキス議長が出席した。

中国財政省の発表によると、藍氏は世界経済の不均衡について、「経済構造に関わる複雑な問題」であり、地政学や保護主義といった経済以外の要因の影響が強まっていると指摘した。

また「全ての関係者は不均衡を包括的かつ客観的に捉えるべきだ」と述べ、開かれた協力とマクロ経済政策の協調を呼びかけた。

items.title: From worst to best: How IT stocks staged a Rs 2.6 lakh crore revival this week
items.author: Veer Sharma
items.summary: Indian IT stocks staged a sharp comeback this week, adding Rs 2.6 lakh crore in market value as the sector gained 12% to become the best-performing index. Better-than-expected Q2 earnings, positive management commentary and a selloff in AI-linked stocks helped revive sentiment, even as concerns over AI adoption and earnings growth persist.
items.body: Market narratives can change quickly, and this week's performance of IT stocks is a case in point. Improved earnings and a downturn in AI-linked stocks, amid multi-billion-dollar investments failing to generate the returns stakeholders had hoped for, have helped IT stocks add Rs 2.60 lakh crore in market value. The index has risen 12%, making it the best-performing index this week.For the week, Tech Mahindra led the index with a gain of over 16%, followed by Wipro at 13%. TCS, Infosys and HCL Tech each advanced 12%. The rally is significant given that FIIs and other investors had fled IT stocks earlier this year as AI-linked stocks gained momentum amid heightened concerns over slowing demand and earnings.What helped IT flip the script?1.) AI’s $1 trillion plunge - US stocks linked to the artificial intelligence trade fell on Thursday, extending a global sell-off that has wiped out more than $1 trillion in market value from 20 of the world's most valuable AI and semiconductor companies so far this week. Concerns over interest rate hikes, AI financing and intensifying competition weighed on investor sentiment.Tensions flared further after OpenAI told investors last week that its annualised revenue for September was nearly $50 billion, lower than the figure it had indicated earlier, Reuters reported. At a separate event, the company had previously told investors that its September revenue run rate was approaching $70 billion.2.) Q2 earnings come at an opportune time - IT companies have posted better-than-expected earnings. India’s largest player TCS reported 15% year-on-year (YoY) growth in its consolidated net profit at Rs 13,884 crore for the second quarter. The same stood at Rs 12,075 crore a year ago. The Board has declared a second interim dividend of Rs 12 per share for the financial year 2026-27.In constant currency terms, revenue rose 0.5% quarter-on-quarter. Operating margin came in at 24%, while net margin stood at 19%. CEO and MD K Krithivasan said the company saw broad-based growth across international markets and most industry segments.3.) Global giant Accenture forecast growth - At investor day, Accenture’s Chief Executive Officer Julie Sweet pushed to dispel fears that new technology poses a major threat to the consulting industry.“The opportunity is bigger than ever before,” she said. “While AI does have the potential, with AI efficiencies, to impact our business more than ever before, we again believe that ultimately, the new demand that will be created, will far exceed the demand that’s being replaced.” Accenture's commentary is closely watched as an indicator of global demand for technology services.4.) AI’s capital roadblock - Earlier this week, Broadcom’s Hock Tan said capital could become a bigger constraint on AI expansion than shortages of semiconductors, memory chips or electricity. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan echoed the concern, flagging the rising cost of capital and the need for companies investing heavily in AI to demonstrate adequate returns.The warnings come as investors reassess the sustainability of the AI-driven rally amid stretched valuations, intensifying competition and uncertainty over when heavy AI investments will translate into profits. Meanwhile, South Korea’s tech-heavy market plunged over 6% on Tuesday as the selloff in AI-linked stocks deepened.IT stocks outlookVK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said strong results from major IT companies and positive management commentary had triggered a sharp recovery in the IT index, helping the Nifty remain resilient. He added that the improvement could provide fundamental support to the broader market.Axis Securities however remains cautiously optimistic about the IT services sector. For the Indian IT sector, the pace of global AI adoption over the next 2-3 years remains a key concern for earnings growth and valuations.Also read: New CAS rules decoded: What Sebi’s revised framework means for stock market traders However, if questions arise globally around the commercial viability of AI, potentially slowing its rollout, market concerns over Indian IT companies could ease, said Krishna Sanghavi, CIO Equity, Mahindra Manulife Mutual Fund. The sector may remain positive in the near term, supported by improving sentiment and buying interest following HCLTech's results, but after a sharp rally, some profit-booking and volatility cannot be ruled out, said Gaurav Garg, head of research at Lemonn Market desk.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser.
